8e6a1f00cabfd64871bafe5c54632155f16eaeb8.title: Observable Transform Factorization
8e6a1f00cabfd64871bafe5c54632155f16eaeb8.body:
Suppose \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}. Let
\[
F_n(z)=\mathbb E_P[\exp(zZ_n)],\quad
M(z)=\mathbb E_P[\exp(z\eta)],\quad
H_n(z)=\mathbb E_P[\exp(zD_n)],
\]
and let
\[
G_n(z)=\mathbb E_P[Y\exp(zZ_n)],\quad
B_n(z)=\mathbb E_P[b_n(X)\exp(zD_n)].
\]
Then, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)
\]
and
\[
G_n(z)=\theta_0 F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]

c3cc9b32a4bab024b526e58436f77703e2424f01.title: Transform Zero Localization
c3cc9b32a4bab024b526e58436f77703e2424f01.body:
Fix a primitive parameter tuple \(p\), with \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge 2\), and a law \(P\) for \(O=(X,T,Y)\) with treatment residual \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), under the usual measurability and integrability conditions. Suppose that \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:eta-subgaussian}\) and \(\cref{obj:ass:cumulant-separation}\). Define
\[
A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)},
\qquad
R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
\qquad
M(z)=\mathbb E_P[\exp(z\eta)] .
\]
Then there exists \(z_0\in\mathbb C\) such that
\[
|z_0|\le R_0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
M(z_0)=0 .
\]

bc1c92da8f057b4d54979c38e5958bab3deac2a9.title: Exact Contour Identification
bc1c92da8f057b4d54979c38e5958bab3deac2a9.body:
Fix \(p\), \(n\ge 1\), and \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Let \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) be certified bank input data as in \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}\), let \(j\in\{0,\ldots,J\}\), and let \(C_j\) be the positively oriented circle with radius \(\rho_j\) from the certified contour bank. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Residual boundary.)} \(F_n(z)\ne 0\) for every \(z\in C_j\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance disk.)} \(H_n(z)\ne 0\) for every \(z\) on or inside \(C_j\).
\item \textbf{(Positive count.)} \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\theta_0
=
\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)
=
\{N_{C_j}(F_n)\,2\pi i\}^{-1}
\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz .
\]
Here \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)\) and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\) are the contour functional and contour count of \(\cref{obj:def:contour-functional}\).

fc36d9a5f1abbadc3e7b88f6a696ce9c1e179bfa.title: Zero-Based Instrument
fc36d9a5f1abbadc3e7b88f6a696ce9c1e179bfa.body:
Fix \(n\ge 1\) and a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Let \(M(z)=E_P[\exp(z\eta)]\), let \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), and let \(H_n(z)\) be the moment generating function of the learned treatment-error term in \(Z_n=\eta+D_n\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive order.)} \(\ell\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Zero and multiplicity.)} \(z_0\in\mathbb C\) satisfies \(M(z_0)=0\), and the analytic order of \(M\) at \(z_0\) is \(\ell\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument.)} \(J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}\exp(z_0w)\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:zero-instrument}\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(d\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)\right]=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X\right]=0
\quad P\text{-a.s.},
\]
and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]
=
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\neq 0\),
\[
\theta_0
=
\frac{E_P\!\left[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]}
     {E_P\!\left[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]}.
\]

55d898087eecbbbac49950df9daf626c89740eb1.title: Certified Contour Bank
55d898087eecbbbac49950df9daf626c89740eb1.body:
Fix the primitive parameter record, the positive certified-real input record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}\), an index \(n\) with \(n\ge 1\), and a law \(P\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as specified by \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).  Let \(B\) be the contour-bank data computed from \((p,\mathfrak p_{\star})\), with constants
\[
 U_{\psi},\ U_R,\ N_{\mathrm{cert}},\ m_{\star},\ d_{\star},\ h_{\star},\
 e_{\star},\ d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}},\ u_{\star},\ a_{\star,\mathbb Q},\ a_{\star}
\]
and radii \(\rho_j\).

Then \(a_{\star}>0\), the radii are strictly increasing, and the computed constants satisfy
\[
\begin{gathered}
N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3,\qquad
m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,\qquad
J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1,\\
d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad
h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,\qquad
e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,\\
d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),\qquad
u_{\star}=2e_{\star}+N_{\mathrm{cert}}\bigl(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}\bigr),\qquad
a_{\star,\mathbb Q}=2^{-u_{\star}} .
\end{gathered}
\]
Moreover, every bank radius lies in the annulus
\[
 R_0<\rho_j<R_1 .
\]
For the treatment-noise transform \(M\) associated with \(P\), there is a bank index \(j\) such that the circle \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\) contains a positive number of zeros of \(M\) in its interior and has the certified boundary modulus
\[
 a_{\star}\le |M(z)|\qquad\text{for every }z\in C_j .
\]

689c8b0783ce391506dcc4423e3045fd9550981f.title: Hard Gaussian Submodel
689c8b0783ce391506dcc4423e3045fd9550981f.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_0,\qquad 0<C_0,\qquad 0<\tau\le \psi_{\xi},\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]
For every parameter tuple \(p\) whose coordinates satisfy
\[
p.r=r,\quad p.\delta=\delta,\quad p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p.C_g=C_g,\quad p.C_q=C_q,\quad
p.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},
\]
and for every \(n\ge 1\), the following assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian path.)} If the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) is nonempty, then there exist a base law \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a one-dimensional family \(\{P_{\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(\theta_0(P_{\vartheta})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and the clipped supplied codes satisfy
\[
\bar g_n(P_{\vartheta})=\bar g_n(P^\circ),
\qquad
\bar q_n(P_{\vartheta})=\bar q_n(P^\circ).
\]
Moreover, under \(P_{\vartheta}\), the outcome innovation \(\xi\) has distribution \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely. For every \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(ACE path.)} For every base law \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\), there exists a one-dimensional family \(\{P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), \(\theta_0(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the treatment noise \(\eta\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), the clipped supplied codes agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and the treatment- and outcome-code \(L^r\) radius conditions hold at \(n\). Under \(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\), the innovation \(\xi\) has distribution \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely. For every \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed-code ACE risk.)} For every pair of clipped code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n(P^\circ)=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n(P^\circ)=\bar q\), then the minimax mean-squared risk over the corresponding fixed-code subclass satisfies
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g,\ \bar q_n(P)=\bar q}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\bigl(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2\right].
\]
\end{itemize}

8a80ddd38616666212cf5a7d34d14147c8c07b4f.title: Symmetric Mixture Reduction
8a80ddd38616666212cf5a7d34d14147c8c07b4f.body:
Fix real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\). There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds. Let \(p\) be any admissible parameter tuple with sample size \(n\), with these four constants equal to \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), respectively, and let \(P\) be any observed-data law. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Symmetric mixture noise.)} The law of \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) under \(P\) is
\[
\tfrac12 N(-1,1)+\tfrac12 N(1,1).
\]
\item \textbf{(Sampling and independence.)} The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) satisfy \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, and the law satisfies \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Ranges and tails.)} The law satisfies \cref{obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}.
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code accuracy.)} The supplied treatment code satisfies
\[
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{1,n},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the fourth cumulant and the treatment-noise transform obey
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=-2,
\qquad
M(i\pi/2)=0,
\]
and, writing \(Z_n\) for the learned residual and \(D_n\) for the treatment-code error,
\[
E_P\!\left[
Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)
\right]
=
e^{-\pi^2/8}
E_P\!\left[
\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)
\right],
\]
with
\[
\frac{e^{-\pi^2/8}}{2}
\le
E_P\!\left[
Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)
\right].
\]
Moreover, the clipped sine-ratio estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\) from \cref{obj:def:sine-estimator} satisfies
\[
E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n}.
\]

81cf9f8aaf2d936aa8dfbf15dd4a02d109104260.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
81cf9f8aaf2d936aa8dfbf15dd4a02d109104260.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have these fixed values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix the primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same fixed values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and with common supplied radii \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and write \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\) for the clipped pair. Suppose that \(n_j=p_j.n\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j;\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\neq\varnothing,\qquad
n_j\ge 2,\qquad
\varepsilon_{1,n_j}\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_gR_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\), depending only on the fixed primitive constants and records, such that, with
\(B\) the translated-dyadic contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\) the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the same transported primitive records, and
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\mathfrak R_{n_j}^{\mathrm{NG}}(p_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
Moreover, the same statistic witnesses the upper bound:
\[
\sup_{P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j;\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), whenever the clipped-code intersection of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty,
\[
\mathfrak R_{p.n}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\mathfrak M_{p.n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

e1b2d82e18eda119f2512f25533be8430dc24193.title: ACE Spectral Alignment
e1b2d82e18eda119f2512f25533be8430dc24193.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) be the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator carried by a fixed published ACE handle.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad
p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad
p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under the common clipped-code convention, the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\) implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(s=r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} If \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4R_1(p)\exp(2C_gR_1(p))\}^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1(p)\) is the search radius from the certified contour bank.  Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds, and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

f91d9b6149f723faa138e5088726b1f86961048c.title: Adaptive Root-n Minimaxity
f91d9b6149f723faa138e5088726b1f86961048c.body:
Fix an integer \(r\ge 2\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}>0\).  There exist constants
\(c,C>0\), depending only on these seven displayed quantities, with the following
property.

Let \(X\) be any measurable covariate space.  Let \(p_0\) be any parameter record
whose fields \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) equal the
displayed constants, and let the remaining fields of \(p_0\) satisfy the standing
parameter requirements: \(n\ge 1\), \(k=r+1\), \(s\ge r\), \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\),
\(\sigma>0\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences
\(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) on positive indices.  Fix
experiment-wide certified bank and range records for \(p_0\).  Let \(p\) be any
parameter record sharing with \(p_0\) the same values of
\(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and let \(P_{\mathrm{base}}\)
be any model over \(p\), under the usual measurability, probability, conditional
mean, and integrability conditions.  Write \(n=p.n\), and let the fixed records be
transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\) in the canonical way.  Let
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) be the statistic of
\(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) built from these transported fixed
records and the supplied treatment-code sequence of \(P_{\mathrm{base}}\).

Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Measurability and represented execution.)}
The statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is measurable.  Moreover, for
every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical
build-and-compilation contract for the same parameter record, transported fixed
records, and supplied treatment-code sequence, the represented-data execution
corresponding to \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is realized.

\item \textbf{(Class relations.)}
Every model in the published ACE comparison class
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\)
belongs to the non-Gaussian spectral class
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).  If the
comparison exponent in \(p\) satisfies \(s=r\), then
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is exactly the subclass
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of
\(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\).

\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code risk.)}
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{NG}}\) be the set of models satisfying
\(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) at index \(n\) whose clipped supplied
treatment and outcome codes agree at index \(n\) with those of
\(P_{\mathrm{base}}\).  If the i.i.d. sampling condition
\(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\) holds for \(P_{\mathrm{base}}\), if
\(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{NG}}\) is nonempty, if \(n\ge 2\), and if
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\bigl(4\,R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\bigr)^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1\) is the search radius determined by the parameter record \(p\), then
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n}\right)
\le
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}},
\]
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{NG}}}
E_P\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right],
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{NG}}}
E_P\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n}\right),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{NG}}}
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(
  \left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|
\right)\right)
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}}\right).
\]

\item \textbf{(ACE fixed-code risk.)}
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}\) be the set of models satisfying
\(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) at index \(n\) whose clipped supplied treatment
and outcome codes agree at index \(n\) with those of \(P_{\mathrm{base}}\).  If
\(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}\) is nonempty, if \(n\ge 2\), and if
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\bigl(4\,R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\bigr)^{-1},
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n}\right)
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}}
E_P\!\left[
  \bigl(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right],
\]
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}}
E_P\!\left[
  \bigl(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}}
E_P\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right],
\]
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}}
E_P\!\left[
  \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n}\right),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{ACE}}}
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(
  \left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|
\right)\right)
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}}\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

f077e91f649a4b955fbf9f71658b9237223f1170.title: Uniform Transform Error

bb6c39899d1cb20f30642b9faf1fd5531c8357c9.title: Zero-Free Nuisance Factor
bb6c39899d1cb20f30642b9faf1fd5531c8357c9.body:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), the associated treatment-code discrepancy \(D_n\) obeys
\[
 |D_n|\le 2C_g\quad\text{almost surely},
 \qquad
 E_P|D_n|\le \varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
Consequently, for the corresponding factor \(H_n\) and radius \(R_1\),
\[
 \sup_{|z|\le R_1}|H_n(z)-1|
 \le R_1 e^{2C_gR_1}\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]
If \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\), then \(|H_n(z)|\ge 3/4\) for every \(|z|\le R_1\), and \(F_n=M H_n\) and \(M\) have the same zeros in \(\{|z|\le R_1\}\), counted with multiplicity.

9ee8441174346b2376e43b98b2e294ed6a3d0b15.title: Gaussian Class Degeneracy
9ee8441174346b2376e43b98b2e294ed6a3d0b15.body:
Fix any admissible parameter tuple \(p\), with sample size \(n=p.n\), satisfying its primitive restrictions: \(n\ge 1\), \(k=r+1\), \(r\ge 2\), \(s\ge r\), \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) on positive indices. Then every law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} has
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
Moreover, for any externally supplied code sequences \(g_{\mathrm{code}}\) and \(q_{\mathrm{code}}\), if there exists at least one law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) whose clipped treatment and outcome codes at index \(n\) agree pointwise with
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{g_{\mathrm{code},n}(x),-C_g\},C_g\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{q_{\mathrm{code},n}(x),-C_q\},C_q\},
\]
respectively, then the corresponding Gaussian minimax MSE and Gaussian minimax generalized-quantile risk are
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]

88f28fd5c102a6b7c4708b40083e4aa39586667f.title: Local Gaussian Benchmarks
88f28fd5c102a6b7c4708b40083e4aa39586667f.body:
Let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge 1}\) be a positive nonincreasing real sequence with \(\delta_n\to0\).  Fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\in\mathbb R\).  The following two assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple with \(p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta}\), \(p.C_g=C_g\), \(p.C_q=C_q\), \(p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}\), \(k=4\), and \(r=3\).  For any \(a\in(0,1]\) and any law \(P\) in a model \(m\), assume that the treatment noise satisfies
\[
\eta\sim \sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Assume also \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}, and assume the treatment-code radius condition at sample size \(n\).  Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path benchmark conclusion holds with constant \(C\) for \(p,m,a\).

\item \textbf{(Local ACE oracle envelope.)} For every published ACE handle, every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and every \(C_{\gamma}\in\mathbb R\), if the handle satisfies the JMS ACE theorem-five-four conclusion at \((\gamma,C_{\gamma})\), then \(C_{\gamma}>0\) and the following local ACE statement holds.  For every parameter tuple \(p\) with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), if \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}>0\), then for every deterministic treatment code \(gcode\), deterministic outcome code \(qcode\), and model \(m\), whenever
\[
\bar g_n=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}gcode_n,
\qquad
\bar q_n=\Pi_{[-C_q,C_q]}qcode_n,
\]
the law belongs to the local JMS ACE class at threshold \(\delta_n\), and the local JMS eligibility condition at threshold \(\delta_n\) holds, the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}
\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}(\delta_n;C_{\gamma}),
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}(\delta_n;C_{\gamma})
=
\mathrm{jmsBound}(p,n,C_{\gamma},\delta_n).
\]
Moreover, for all real numbers \(risk,U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), if \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{DML}}\) and \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), then
\[
risk\le \min\{U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

d0f71e3e54e0a5c2300e820396ac0f2fe462c648.title: ACE Class Relations
d0f71e3e54e0a5c2300e820396ac0f2fe462c648.body:
Fix any admissible parameter vector in the sense of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class,obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}, with ACE order \(r\), comparison exponent \(s\), and any class index \(n\). For every observed-data law \(P\) on a measurable covariate space, equipped with the supplied clipped codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\),
\[
P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
If \(s=r\), then for every such law \(P\),
\[
P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]

9a50afb77ea9074fc817e5c14850a78444061478.title: Gaussian-Rademacher Sine Benchmark
9a50afb77ea9074fc817e5c14850a78444061478.body:
Fix real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\).  There is a constant \(C>0\), depending on these four constants alone, such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be an admissible parameter tuple with sample size \(n\), with
\[
p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad p.C_g=C_g,\qquad p.C_q=C_q,\qquad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\qquad p.k=4,
\]
and let \(a\in(0,1]\).  For any observed-data law \(P\), write
\[
\eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,\qquad
t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},\qquad
A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\) and \(S\) are independent.  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Path law.)} The treatment noise satisfies \(\eta\sim\eta_a\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).
\item \textbf{(Independence and mean restriction.)} The law satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise}\) and \(\cref{obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence}\).
\item \textbf{(Ranges and tail envelope.)} The law satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code radius at \(n\).)} With \(\bar g_n\) denoting the clipped supplied treatment code,
\[
\int |\bar g_n(x)-g_0(x)|\,dP_X(x)\le \varepsilon_{1,n},
\]
under the usual integrability condition for this \(L^1(P_X)\) quantity.
\end{itemize}
Define \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) and \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\).  Then the treatment-noise moment-generating function and fourth cumulant along this path are
\[
M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
\qquad
\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4 .
\]
Moreover \(t_a>0\), \(M_a(it_a)=0\), \(M_a(iu)\ne0\) for every \(u\in(0,t_a)\), and for every real \(d\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\sin\{t_a(\eta+d)\}\right]=0 .
\]
If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/2\), then
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]
=
A_a\,\mathbb E_P\!\left[\cos(t_aD_n)\right]
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbb E_P\!\left[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)\right]\ge A_a/2 .
\]
For the estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_{a,n}
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
\frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
     {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
&\displaystyle \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
the same condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/2\) implies
\[
\mathbb E_{P^n}\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2\right]
\le
C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n a^{-2}
\exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, with \(\Delta_a=2a^4\), the condition entails
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le \frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi}
\]
and the risk bound can be written as
\[
\mathbb E_{P^n}\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2\right]
\le
C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\}.
\]

c299cc01fac64b1c3e17c05ad62621e4c0568e51.title: Independent treatment noise
c299cc01fac64b1c3e17c05ad62621e4c0568e51.body:
The treatment innovation is independent of the covariates:
\[
\eta\perp X.
\]

5de98add0524f390abb6f51e586378283ac4f36c.title: Outcome mean independence
5de98add0524f390abb6f51e586378283ac4f36c.body:
The outcome innovation has zero conditional mean:
\[
E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0
\]
almost surely.

a8cea20412629cc03dbab92c8a60a908b4d12e2e.title: Target range
a8cea20412629cc03dbab92c8a60a908b4d12e2e.body:
The partially linear coefficient satisfies
\[
|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}.
\]

a39521e4df34a3a8f4d1baee0910ee3b197b5580.title: Treatment regression range
a39521e4df34a3a8f4d1baee0910ee3b197b5580.body:
The treatment regression function satisfies
\[
\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g.
\]

e749039676b008b316d856f23aeca3bd1d24af18.title: Outcome regression range
e749039676b008b316d856f23aeca3bd1d24af18.body:
The outcome regression function satisfies
\[
\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q.
\]

023f3be49d50fbfb347bf9a6a526f9395c8ecd49.title: Bounded Gaussian Outcome
023f3be49d50fbfb347bf9a6a526f9395c8ecd49.body:
The outcome satisfies
\[
|Y|\le C_q
\]
almost surely.

2c8d60fb10e546181331b3b07596d49f077444cd.title: Treatment Noise Sub-Gaussianity
2c8d60fb10e546181331b3b07596d49f077444cd.body:
With the Luxemburg convention
\[
\lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
=
\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment noise satisfies
\[
\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}.
\]

16faa6f82deb7edec9e7bfd0c906aa02d8f9eca9.title: Outcome Innovation Sub-Gaussianity
16faa6f82deb7edec9e7bfd0c906aa02d8f9eca9.body:
The outcome innovation satisfies
\[
\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}
\]
almost surely.

f35fc18621bc1cab496e1667a0a4053874c79ea3.title: Cumulant Separation
f35fc18621bc1cab496e1667a0a4053874c79ea3.body:
The \(k\)th cumulant of the treatment noise satisfies
\[
|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta.
\]

7cf7b71ebdf8e6c4b54a3468adfe30182278361e.title: Gaussian treatment noise
7cf7b71ebdf8e6c4b54a3468adfe30182278361e.body:
The treatment innovation is Gaussian:
\[
\eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

eea2073949eab5701f9fcc0a67426a0af184d253.title: Non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\)
eea2073949eab5701f9fcc0a67426a0af184d253.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation}\), let \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) be the class of observed-data laws \(P\) for \(O=(X,T,Y)\) whose residual functionals \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment noise.)} \(\eta\perp X\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome mean.)} \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Target range.)} \(|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment regression range.)} \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome regression range.)} \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment innovation envelope.)} \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome innovation envelope.)} \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code accuracy.)} \(\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}
=
\left\{
P:
\begin{array}{l}
\eta\perp X,\quad E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\quad |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\\
\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g,\quad \lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q,\\
\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\quad
\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\\
|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\quad
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]

8cdcaed70ffdb7b682cb8e8c06a9eb65097b11a9.title: Gaussian JMS class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)
8cdcaed70ffdb7b682cb8e8c06a9eb65097b11a9.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:bounded-gaussian-outcome,obj:ass:gaussian-treatment-noise}\), let \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) be the class of observed-data laws \(P\) whose residual functionals \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Outcome mean.)} \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Target range.)} \(|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Bounded outcome.)} \(|Y|\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment noise.)} \(\eta\perp X\) and \(\eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment regression range.)} \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code accuracy.)} \(\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome-code accuracy.)} \(\lVert \bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
=
\left\{
P:
\begin{array}{l}
E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\quad |\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\quad |Y|\le C_q,\\
\eta\perp X,\quad \eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2),\quad
\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g,\\
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\quad
\lVert \bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]

780065c9662751bec2edffb519ead1674cd7e1ec.title: JMS ACE comparison class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)
780065c9662751bec2edffb519ead1674cd7e1ec.body:
The JMS ACE comparison class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) consists of all observed-data laws \(P\) for which the residual functionals \(g_0,q_0,\eta,\xi\) determined by \(P\) satisfy \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation}\) and
\[
\begin{gathered}
E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\qquad
|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\qquad
\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\qquad
\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\\
\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\qquad
\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\qquad
\eta\perp X,\qquad
|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\\
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\qquad
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^r(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\end{gathered}
\]

a16fe3b2e415797878dd54045ce27c40659a5fa2.title: Zero instrument \(J_{z_0,\ell}\)
a16fe3b2e415797878dd54045ce27c40659a5fa2.body:
Given a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) with multiplicity \(\ell\), define
\[
J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}.
\]

c3d19724027a501e8e92cd9ef49e88576ab5b163.title: Contour functional \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)\)
c3d19724027a501e8e92cd9ef49e88576ab5b163.body:
For a positively oriented circle \(C_j\) on which \(F_n\) is zero-free and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge 1\), define
\[
\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)
=
\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}
\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz .
\]

48894a60e25381e46c3a9d1053c11205c9fc7297.title: Minimax risks \(\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}},\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G},\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}\)

5214711748d82e4363473082625801db577c7a83.title: JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)
5214711748d82e4363473082625801db577c7a83.body:
Let \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\) be the JMS eligibility quantities. On indices for which the displayed expressions are defined, \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is the condition
\[
r
\le
\min\left\{
\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}
-
a_{1,n}^{-1}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
\frac{b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2b_{2,n})}
\right\}.
\]

0e5d3c8b3b9ee2a21ea00a01e342fa46b06badf4.title: Sine-ratio estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\)

fbf583ccf363bf01c8c66b1ef21a09df8754ff1b.title: Local Gaussian handle \(\mathscr C_m\)

39423cb90dada12b1b162283a01a0471d6f3dce4.title: ACE comparison class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)
39423cb90dada12b1b162283a01a0471d6f3dce4.body:
Relative to \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), define
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) retains every condition of the broad spectral class and imposes both supplied-code restrictions in \(L^s(P_X)\).

d91719eefd1fa0e32bc2fe3717234847abfa4ff7.title: Certified contour substrate \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\)
d91719eefd1fa0e32bc2fe3717234847abfa4ff7.body:
The paper-independent bounded-build obligation \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) is the following finite implementation specification. A certified real record consists of rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic contract
\[
 x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
 \qquad
 I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e.
\]
A positive record additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) with \(p\le x\). Executable code inspects the interval, modulus, and positivity fields.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
 A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
 \qquad
 A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
\[
 A B=
 [\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
  \max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\). Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are implemented by these endpoint operations and
\[
 (A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), put
\[
 \operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
 \min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Then \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by the rational interval obtained by adding the corresponding square bounds. Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures; after \(q\) bisections, their width is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\). This supplies certified modulus lower and upper bounds. Division is the guarded operation
\[
 \frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
 =(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
executed when the modulus routine has returned a rational lower bound \(m>0\); outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\) is then sound.

The certified name of \(\pi\) is constructed from Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\), the first \(N+1\) terms of
\[
 \arctan x=\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R_N(x),
 \qquad
 |R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3},
\]
give rational nested enclosures after intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested enclosures. If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the explicit choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\), giving an effective modulus with finite fuel.

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations. The Lagrange remainders are bounded respectively by
\[
 3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
 \qquad
 \frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
 N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\). Since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this displayed \(N\) gives a sound error at most \(e\). Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested. Hence
\[
 \exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle. Combining the constructed \(\pi\) name with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius record \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\), \(0\le q<N\), certified circle-node records for
\[
 r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive. If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), a uniform mesh with
\[
 N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell. Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the displayed finite number of operations yields sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures. Their fuel consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and a finite number of endpoint operations. Absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) by implementing these algorithms, exporting their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiling the resulting module. This definition is the explicit bounded-build obligation. Later executable conclusions are conditional on a build satisfying this specification.

f066c7f0d10ec371e079736792c554ccd2e4bd31.title: Contour bank handle \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\)
f066c7f0d10ec371e079736792c554ccd2e4bd31.body:
Let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote an actually supplied positive certified-real record satisfying the bounded-build substrate specification. As part of the experiment convention, fix once for all the single actual record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k,\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k\) is exact and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1),
\]
with the value contracts
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Each positive name includes its rational positivity witness. The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and it is the primitive record used by both the bank and the estimator. The construction reads its supplied interval, modulus, and positivity fields.

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one. If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), put
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1.
\]
For \(q=0,\ldots,2^{m_{\star}-1}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record for \(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_q
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
Its value is \(\rho_q=R_0+1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\). Enumerate these radii increasingly and set
\[
 C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}.
\]

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),
\]
\[
 u_{\star}=2e_{\star}
 +N_{\mathrm{cert}}(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}>0.
\]
Every output datum is obtained by the displayed finite modulus calls, rational endpoint operations, and primitive recursion over displayed integer bounds. The construction is a bounded finite procedure using the identical fixed record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), which gives the same bank and certificate for every \(n\). The universal guarantee is stated separately.

5f8fbe4d8f3aed904cde2227c5717dc68fd33437.title: Adaptive contour statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\)
5f8fbe4d8f3aed904cde2227c5717dc68fd33437.body:
The construction has a mathematical layer and a represented-data layer, both relative to exactly the same experiment-wide primitive records.

Fix the record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) from the contour-bank handle and, once for all, fix one actual record
\[
 \mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(C_{\theta}).
\]
These records are fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and they remain the primitive names used throughout the construction.

At the mathematical layer, for an ordinary real observation coordinate set
\[
 \mathcal I_m(x)=
 \left[2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
       2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}\right],
 \qquad m\ge1.
\]
Canonicalize \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\) through these floor-dyadic records. Run the finite rational procedure below with those observation records and with the already fixed, unchanged records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\), and take the value represented by its output record. This defines \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as a total map on ordinary real samples relative to the fixed full primitive record. The canonical observation digits are part of this mathematical interpretation.

At the represented-data layer, the full input record is
\[
 \mathfrak s_{\star}=
 \bigl((\mathfrak t_i,\mathfrak y_i,\mathfrak g_i)_{i=1}^n,
       \mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathfrak t_i\), \(\mathfrak y_i\), and \(\mathfrak g_i\) are supplied canonical digital records for \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\). The transducer is defined relative to the displayed fixed primitive components. A transducer exists at this layer relative to a concrete implementation that has been added and compiled with all contracts of the bounded-build substrate. It reads the represented input fields specified here.

Invoke the contour-bank handle on \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and form \(\mathfrak z_i=\mathfrak t_i-\mathfrak g_i\) by certified subtraction. At every certified circle node, use the substrate's complex rectangle operations and nested complex-exponential extension to construct, by finite sums, enclosures of
\[
 \widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
 \widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
 =|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
 \quad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Every node precision is obtained by applying the compositional modulus to a rational error budget.

For explicit mesh fuel, refine each observation record at error one and take the resulting rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\). Use \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\) to turn the finite empirical derivative sums into rational bounds for all functions below. With \(z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it}\), put
\[
 W_{0j}(t)=
 \rho_je^{2\pi it}
 \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))},
\]
and, after a positive integer \(N_j\) has been certified,
\[
 V_j(t)=
 \frac{\rho_je^{2\pi it}}{N_j}
 \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
      {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
If a rational lower modulus certificate is \(m>0\), use
\[
 |W'_{0j}(t)|\le
 2\pi\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
 \right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 |V'_j(t)|\le
 \frac{2\pi}{N_j}\left[
 \rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\rho_j^2\left\{
 \frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
 +\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
 \right\}\right].
\]
For a rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational bound \(L\), take the mesh size \(\lceil L/e\rceil+1\), and allocate node error by the finite number of operations. Thus every precision and mesh has displayed finite fuel.

On the pilot fold, compute for every \(j\) a sound interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing \(\inf_{C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}|\). If its lower endpoint \(m_j\) is positive, guarded division and finite quadrature enclose
\[
 \int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\). Record \(N_j\) exactly when the real interval contains a unique nonnegative integer and the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject the circle. A circle is admissible exactly when \(m_j\ge a_{\star}/2\) and \(N_j\ge1\). Select an admissible circle having the greatest rational lower endpoint, with smallest-index tie-break, and return the certified zero name if none exists.

On the evaluation fold, compute the analogous modulus enclosure and return the certified zero name if its lower endpoint is below \(a_{\star}/4\). Otherwise guarded division and finite quadrature give a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
 \int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
 =\frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
   \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the rational midpoint of its real interval, represented by its rational point name. Projection uses certified addition, subtraction, multiplication by \(1/2\), and the interval absolute-value operation to construct a certified name whose value is
\[
 \operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
 =\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
 =\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
This certified-real name is the transducer output.

An execution trace is the finite list of input-modulus calls, returned precisions, Taylor and square-root cutoffs, mesh sizes, rational rectangle operations, guarded divisions, rational endpoint comparisons, fallback decisions, and the tie-break. Identical full input records \(\mathfrak s_{\star}\), including their fixed primitive components, have identical traces and output records. The value represented by that output is, by definition, the ordinary-sample Borel statistic evaluated with the same fixed primitive records. The procedure uses \(\bar g_n\). The represented-data transducer and its compiled computability conclusion are conditional on completing the bounded-build obligation; the ordinary-sample Borel statistic and its statistical risk are mathematical objects independently of that build status.

e8fe727ec39d3b71eabb35a008010cbe63e87acf.title: Local-to-Gaussian frontier
e8fe727ec39d3b71eabb35a008010cbe63e87acf.body: For triangular treatment-noise laws with \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\downarrow0\) under the same supplied code sequences, it remains open whether a data-driven selector among ordinary DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour procedures can attain the sharp minimax mean-squared-error rate as a function of \((n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n)\), yield uniformly valid inference across these regimes, and admit a matching local minimax lower bound. A full resolution would specify the sharp-rate functional, the uniform-inference or coverage criterion, the selector, the confidence procedure, and the matching lower-bound witness.

630c9ed3331f70b702a379d22a0aee6edeb0be63.title: Zero Localization Radius
630c9ed3331f70b702a379d22a0aee6edeb0be63.body:
Fix a primitive parameter tuple \(p\) and a model \(P\) for \(O=(X,T,Y)\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} The cumulant order satisfies \(k=r+1\) with \(r\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Innovation.)} The treatment innovation is \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), under the usual measurability and integrability conditions.
\item \textbf{(Sub-Gaussian envelope.)} The treatment innovation satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:eta-subgaussian}\) with scale \(\psi_{\eta}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} The same law satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:cumulant-separation}\) with separation \(\delta\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
A_k=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)},
\qquad
R_0=A_k(\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
\qquad
M(z)=\mathbb E_P[\exp(z\eta)] .
\]
Then there exists \(z_0\in\mathbb C\) such that
\[
|z_0|\le R_0
\qquad
M(z_0)=0 .
\]

9f8a3ba2030ad975fdb06369cd4de906ffbbbae8.title: Gaussian hard submodel
9f8a3ba2030ad975fdb06369cd4de906ffbbbae8.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_0,\qquad 0<C_0,\qquad 0<\tau\le \psi_{\xi},\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]
For every parameter tuple \(p\) with
\[
p.r=r,\quad p.\delta=\delta,\quad p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p.C_g=C_g,\quad p.C_q=C_q,\quad
p.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},
\]
and every \(n\ge 1\), if \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) from \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} is nonempty, then the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian path.)} There exist a base law \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a one-dimensional family \(\{P_{\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(\theta_0(P_{\vartheta})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and
\[
\bar g_n(P_{\vartheta})=\bar g_n(P^\circ),
\qquad
\bar q_n(P_{\vartheta})=\bar q_n(P^\circ).
\]
Under \(P_{\vartheta}\), the outcome innovation \(\xi\) has distribution \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely. For every \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(ACE path.)} For every base law \(P^\circ\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}, there exists a one-dimensional family \(\{P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}, \(\theta_0(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the treatment noise \(\eta\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), the clipped supplied codes agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and the treatment- and outcome-code \(L^r\) radius conditions hold at \(n\). Under \(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\), the innovation \(\xi\) has distribution \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely. For every \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed-code ACE risk.)} For every pair of clipped code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists a law \(P^\circ\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} with \(\bar g_n(P^\circ)=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n(P^\circ)=\bar q\), then the minimax mean-squared risk over laws satisfying \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} with fixed clipped codes \(\bar g_n=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n=\bar q\) satisfies
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\mathfrak R_n\!\left(\{P:\ P \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class},\ \bar g_n(P)=\bar g,\ \bar q_n(P)=\bar q\}\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

2e5752ff1a7bdd338d2863b70bf6135c27337359.title: Non-Gaussian law class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\)
2e5752ff1a7bdd338d2863b70bf6135c27337359.body:
Relative to \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation}, let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \(O=(X,T,Y)\). Define
\[
g_0(x)=\mathbb E_P[T\mid X=x],
\qquad
q_0(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x],
\qquad
\eta=T-g_0(X),
\qquad
\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta .
\]
The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) consists exactly of those laws \(P\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment innovation.)} \(\eta\perp X\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome innovation.)} \(\mathbb E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Parameter and nuisance bounds.)} \(|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), and \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Tail bounds.)} \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\).
\item \textbf{(First-stage proximity.)} \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}
=
\left\{
P:
\begin{array}{l}
\eta\perp X,\quad
\mathbb E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\quad
|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta},\quad
\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g,\quad
\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q,\\
\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\quad
\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\quad
|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\quad
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) is determined entirely by these displayed requirements.

333f6bd32152418242b9a104239c19b22e8cc057.title: Gaussian Hard Submodels
333f6bd32152418242b9a104239c19b22e8cc057.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_0,\qquad 0<C_0,\qquad 0<\tau\le \psi_{\xi},\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]
For every parameter tuple \(p\) with
\[
p.r=r,\quad p.\delta=\delta,\quad p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p.C_g=C_g,\quad p.C_q=C_q,\quad
p.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},
\]
and every \(n\ge 1\), the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian path.)} If the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) is nonempty, then there exist a base law \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a family \(\{P_\vartheta:\vartheta\in\mathbb R\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_\vartheta\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(\theta_0(P_\vartheta)=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_\vartheta\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and
\[
\bar g_n(P_\vartheta)=\bar g_n(P^\circ),
\qquad
\bar q_n(P_\vartheta)=\bar q_n(P^\circ).
\]
Under \(P_\vartheta\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_\vartheta)\eta\), with \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), has distribution \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and satisfies
\[
Y=q_0^{\circ}(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely, where \(q_0^{\circ}\) is the outcome regression of \(P^\circ\). For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(ACE path.)} For every base law \(P^\circ\) in the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\), there exists a family \(\{P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}}:\vartheta\in\mathbb R\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), \(\theta_0(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and
\[
\bar g_n(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\bar g_n(P^\circ),
\qquad
\bar q_n(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\bar q_n(P^\circ).
\]
The treatment-code and outcome-code \(L^r\) radius conditions hold at \(n\) for \(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}}\). Under \(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}}\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_\vartheta^{\mathrm{ACE}})\eta\) has distribution \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and satisfies
\[
Y=q_0^{\circ}(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely, where \(q_0^{\circ}\) is the outcome regression of \(P^\circ\). For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed-code ACE risk.)} For every pair of clipped code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n(P^\circ)=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n(P^\circ)=\bar q\), then the minimax mean-squared risk over the fixed-code subclass satisfies
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g,\ \bar q_n(P)=\bar q}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\bigl(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2\right].
\]
\end{itemize}

455f56fb66056e1259807d0e30ad39c2e3fb4181.title: Non-Gaussian law class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\)
455f56fb66056e1259807d0e30ad39c2e3fb4181.body:
Using the constants and conditions indexed by \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation}, let \(P\) be an observed-data law for \(O=(X,T,Y)\). Define
\[
g_0(x)=E_P[T\mid X=x],
\qquad
q_0(x)=E_P[Y\mid X=x],
\]
let \(\theta_0(P)\) be the constant coefficient in
\[
E_P[Y\mid X,T]=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\{T-g_0(X)\},
\]
and set
\[
\eta=T-g_0(X),
\qquad
\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)\eta .
\]
The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) consists exactly of those laws \(P\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment innovation.)} \(\eta\perp X\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome innovation.)} \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient and nuisance bounds.)} \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\), \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\), and \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Sub-Gaussian tails.)} \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\).
\item \textbf{(First-stage accuracy.)} \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\end{itemize}
Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) is determined by these displayed conditions.

8578256ccde0de969eaee57ee558457f17b130bb.title: Zero instrument \(J_{z_0,\ell}\)
8578256ccde0de969eaee57ee558457f17b130bb.body:
Define the treatment-innovation moment-generating function by
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}].
\]
For a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) with multiplicity \(\ell\), define
\[
J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}.
\]

5a2b1115d05a1620ef783ef7a96d9e053ecd0edf.title: Contour functional \(\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)\)
5a2b1115d05a1620ef783ef7a96d9e053ecd0edf.body:
For \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), define
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{zZ_n}],
\qquad
G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}],
\qquad
H_n(z)=E_P[e^{z\{g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\}}].
\]
Let \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\) denote the number of zeros of \(F_n\) inside the positively oriented circle \(C_j\), counted with multiplicity. When \(F_n\) is zero-free on \(C_j\) and \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge1\), define
\[
\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)
=
\{N_{C_j}(F_n)2\pi i\}^{-1}
\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz .
\]

5f741fee783c16bcb5e392726e9beaf58b03bcbd.title: Non-Gaussian Hard Submodel
5f741fee783c16bcb5e392726e9beaf58b03bcbd.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_0,\qquad 0<C_0,\qquad 0<\tau,\qquad \tau\le \psi_{\xi},\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]
For every parameter tuple \(p\) whose coordinates satisfy
\[
p.r=r,\quad p.\delta=\delta,\quad p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p.C_g=C_g,\quad p.C_q=C_q,\quad
p.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},
\]
and for every \(n\ge 1\), the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian path.)} If the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} is nonempty, then there exist a base law \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a one-dimensional family \(\{P_{\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), \(\theta_0(P_{\vartheta})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and
\[
\bar g_n(P_{\vartheta})=\bar g_n(P^\circ),
\qquad
\bar q_n(P_{\vartheta})=\bar q_n(P^\circ).
\]
Under \(P_{\vartheta}\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{\vartheta})\eta\), with \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and satisfies
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely. For every \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(ACE path.)} For every base law \(P^\circ\) in the JMS ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}, there exists a one-dimensional family \(\{P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that, for every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), \(\theta_0(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\), the law of \((X,T)\) equals its law under \(P^\circ\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the treatment innovation \(\eta\) agree with those of \(P^\circ\), the clipped supplied codes agree with those of \(P^\circ\), and the treatment- and outcome-code \(L^r\) radius conditions hold at \(n\). Under \(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\), the innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})\eta\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\), is independent of \((X,T)\), and
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely. For every \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed-code ACE risk.)} For every pair of clipped code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists \(P^\circ\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n(P^\circ)=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n(P^\circ)=\bar q\), then the minimax mean-squared risk over the corresponding fixed-code subclass satisfies
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g,\ \bar q_n(P)=\bar q}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\bigl(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2\right].
\]
\end{itemize}

fad88cacfd0ea61d0ec7a2fe2a778d6b4de9df39.title: ACE Spectral Alignment
fad88cacfd0ea61d0ec7a2fe2a778d6b4de9df39.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) be the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator carried by a fixed published ACE handle.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad
p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under the common clipped-code convention, the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(s=r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} If \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the eligibility condition of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), the eligibility condition of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4R_1(p)\exp(2C_gR_1(p))\}^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1(p)\) is the search radius from the certified contour bank.  Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), the eligibility condition of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds, and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

8429d7d2066d90b176414d5ac86d08bab8adac94.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
8429d7d2066d90b176414d5ac86d08bab8adac94.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have these values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment records consisting of a certified bank input \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and a certified range input \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)_{j\ge1}\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and with supplied radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\) satisfying
\[
(p_j).\varepsilon_{1,n}=\varepsilon_1,\qquad
(p_j).\varepsilon_{2,n}=\varepsilon_2
\]
for every \(j\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and let its clipped pair be
\[
\bar g_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},\qquad
\bar q_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Write \(n_j=(p_j).n\), and suppose that \(n_j\to\infty\) and that, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\{m:\ m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j)\ \text{of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}},\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{n_j}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
\[
2\le n_j,\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2(p_j).C_gR_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1(p)=R_0(p)+1\). Then there exist constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\) the transported certified bank input for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), and
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
For the same sufficiently large \(j\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, formed from the transported bank and range records and the code \(\widehat g\), is measurable; every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification has its represented execution on these transported records; and
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j)\\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{n_j},\ \bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{n_j}}}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(m)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian fixed-code class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p)\) of \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} satisfies
\[
\theta_0(m)=0.
\]
For every parameter value \(p\) and every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if
\[
\{m:\ m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p),\
\bar G_{p,m,p.n}=\bar g_{p.n},\
\bar Q_{p,m,p.n}=\bar q_{p.n}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

1788601bbdcec54909f09ef3e1a764ee6aad7663.title: ACE Spectral Alignment
1788601bbdcec54909f09ef3e1a764ee6aad7663.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) be the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator carried by a fixed published ACE handle.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad
p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad
p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(p.s=p.r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} For every model \(P\) whose treatment and outcome regressions equal the supplied clipped codes, membership \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the eligibility predicate \(\mathsf E^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p,n)\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility}, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\) imply
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p,n)\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
