\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), \(p_n.r=r\), \(p_n.\delta=\delta\), \(p_n.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta}\), \(p_n.C_g=C_g\), \(p_n.C_q=C_q\), \(p_n.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta}\), \(p_n.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p_n,n)\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds with \(p=p_n\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

15fc8b0368520dccd56e33a49561049ac084a75b.title: ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)
15fc8b0368520dccd56e33a49561049ac084a75b.body:
Relative to \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), define
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},\
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) retains every condition of the broad spectral class and imposes both supplied-code restrictions in \(L^s(P_X)\).

bdd93709b579bbc1f9090743f71239174e21e45a.title: Local Gaussian Benchmarks
bdd93709b579bbc1f9090743f71239174e21e45a.body:
Let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge 1}\) be a positive nonincreasing real sequence with \(\delta_n\to0\), and fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\in\mathbb R\).  The following two assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple with
\[
p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad
p.C_g=C_g,\qquad
p.C_q=C_q,\qquad
p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\qquad
p.k=4,\qquad
p.r=3.
\]
For any \(a\in(0,1]\) and any model \(m\), assume that the treatment innovation satisfies
\[
\eta\sim \sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Assume also \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}, and assume the treatment-code \(L^1\) radius condition at sample size \(p.n\).  Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path benchmark conclusion holds for \(p,m,a\) with constant \(C\).

\item \textbf{(Local ACE oracle envelope.)} For every published ACE handle, every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and every \(C_{\gamma}\in\mathbb R\), if the handle satisfies the JMS ACE theorem-five-four conclusion at \((\gamma,C_{\gamma})\), then \(C_{\gamma}>0\) and the following local ACE bound holds.  For every parameter tuple \(p\) with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\) and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,p.n}>0,\qquad \varepsilon_{2,p.n}>0,
\]
for every deterministic treatment code \(gcode\), deterministic outcome code \(qcode\), and model \(m\), if
\[
\bar g_{p.n}=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}gcode_{p.n},
\qquad
\bar q_{p.n}=\Pi_{[-C_q,C_q]}qcode_{p.n},
\]
the law belongs to the local JMS ACE class at threshold \(\delta_{p.n}\), and the local eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_{p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds at threshold \(\delta_{p.n}\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}
\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},p.r,p.n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\mathrm{jmsBound}(p,p.n,C_{\gamma},\delta_{p.n}).
\]
Moreover, for all real numbers \(risk,U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), if \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{DML}}\) and \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), then
\[
risk\le \min\{U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

9be768f0f9391a03d7bd3a84fbebcfb9b016815b.title: ACE Alignment Bounds
9be768f0f9391a03d7bd3a84fbebcfb9b016815b.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let a published ACE handle supply the order-\(r\) estimator
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\), indexed by \(r\), \(n\), and the supplied treatment and outcome code sequences.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad
p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad
p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same values of
\[
r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}
\]
as \(p_0\), with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(p.s=p.r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} For every model \(P\) whose treatment and outcome regressions equal the supplied clipped codes, membership \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the eligibility predicate \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility}, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\) imply
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds for \(p_n\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds with \(p=p_n\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

31b76bab9757f6bda8bc2652785425ad52346f2a.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
31b76bab9757f6bda8bc2652785425ad52346f2a.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have these values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment records consisting of a certified bank input \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and a certified range input \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter-record sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and with supplied radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\) satisfying
\[
(p_j).\varepsilon_{1,n}=\varepsilon_1,\qquad
(p_j).\varepsilon_{2,n}=\varepsilon_2
\]
for every \(j\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and define the clipped external codes at parameter record \(p\) by
\[
\bar g_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-(p.C_g)\},p.C_g\},\qquad
\bar q_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-(p.C_q)\},p.C_q\}.
\]
Write \(n_j=(p_j).n\). Suppose that \(n_j\to\infty\) and that, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\{m:\ m \text{ satisfies the non-Gaussian class of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} for } p_j \text{ at index } n_j,\ 
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
where \(\bar G_{p,m,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{m.gcode_n(x),-(p.C_g)\},p.C_g\}\) and \(\bar Q_{p,m,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{m.qcode_n(x),-(p.C_q)\},p.C_q\}\). Suppose also that, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
2\le n_j,\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2(p_j).C_gR_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1},
\]
with \(R_1(p)=R_0(p)+1\). Then there exist constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\) the transported certified bank input for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), and
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
For the same sufficiently large \(j\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, formed from the transported bank and range records and the code \(\widehat g\), is measurable; every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification has its represented execution on these transported records; and
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\text{ satisfies the non-Gaussian class of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} for }p_j\text{ at }n_j\\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\ \bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}}}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(m)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian fixed-code class.)} For every parameter record \(p\), every model \(m\) satisfying the Gaussian class of \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} for \(p\) at index \(p.n\) has
\[
\theta_0(m)=0.
\]
For every parameter record \(p\) and every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if
\[
\{m:\ m \text{ satisfies the Gaussian class of \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} for }p\text{ at index }p.n,\ 
\bar G_{p,m,p.n}=\bar g_{p,p.n},\
\bar Q_{p,m,p.n}=\bar q_{p,p.n}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

e94ed2c074eb8f507b5eb27df916b17be1df733b.title: Fixed-code Gaussian minimax risk \(\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(n;\widehat g,\widehat q)\)
e94ed2c074eb8f507b5eb27df916b17be1df733b.body:
For supplied nuisance codes \(\widehat g\) and \(\widehat q\), define the fixed-code Gaussian-intersection class by
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:
g_P^{\mathrm{clip}}=\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}
\ \text{and}\
q_P^{\mathrm{clip}}=\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}
\right\}.
\]
The corresponding minimax risk is
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(n;\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\!\left[
\left(
\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\theta_0(P)
\right)^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum ranges over measurable estimators
\(\widetilde\theta:\mathcal O^n\to\mathbb R\).

ad2c75082911195588eef900a4eb553ac23e9bf3.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
ad2c75082911195588eef900a4eb553ac23e9bf3.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}>0\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have the fixed values \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix the primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same fixed values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and with supplied radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon_2\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and write \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\) for its clipping to \([-C_g,C_g]\) and \([-C_q,C_q]\). Suppose that \(n_j=p_j.n\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j;\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\neq\varnothing,\qquad
n_j\ge 2,\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_gR_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the translated-dyadic contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\mathrm{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n_j}\right)
\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\mathrm{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right).
\]
Moreover, the same statistic witnesses the upper bound:
\[
\sup_{P\in \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j;\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\mathrm{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right).
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} satisfies
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), whenever the clipped-code Gaussian intersection is nonempty,
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

1e28de69f0db3867609136f4eeb7a762b0dd0f74.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
1e28de69f0db3867609136f4eeb7a762b0dd0f74.body:

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every law in the

For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if the

If

743eb194aa8da5edb7277d7cb8f6f481cf3066e9.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
743eb194aa8da5edb7277d7cb8f6f481cf3066e9.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}>0\). For every measurable
covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) be any parameter vector with fixed
values \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix primitive records
\(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in
\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let
\((p_j)_{j\ge 1}\) be any parameter sequence with the same fixed values
\(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and whose supplied
radius schedules are exactly \(\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon_2\). Let
\((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair. For a model
\(M\) at \((p,n)\), write
\[
\bar G_{p,M,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{g^M_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
\bar Q_{p,M,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{q^M_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\},
\]
where \(g^M_n\) and \(q^M_n\) are the deterministic codes carried by \(M\). For the
externally supplied code pair, write
\[
\bar g_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
\bar q_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Put \(n_j=p_j.n\). Suppose that \(n_j\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\{M\in\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\text{ at }(p_j,n_j):
\bar G_{p_j,M,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\ 
\bar Q_{p_j,M,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
\[
n_j\ge 2,
\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_j)
\exp\{2\,C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from
\(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported
primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of
\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} is measurable, every compiled bounded
spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is
represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n_j}\right)
\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{\substack{
M\in\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\text{ at }(p_j,n_j)\\
\bar G_{p_j,M,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\ 
\bar Q_{p_j,M,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}
}}
\mathbb E_M\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(M)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right).
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model in
\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at sample size \(p.n\) satisfies
\[
\theta_0=0.
\]
For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if the
corresponding clipped-code Gaussian intersection is nonempty, then
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

81656ae7e323bf05aa47c1d91e1f1dca67ad928f.title: Minimax quantile risk $\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}$
81656ae7e323bf05aa47c1d91e1f1dca67ad928f.body:
We define \(\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)\) by
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\ \bar g_{p.n}=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}\widehat g_{p.n},\ \bar q_{p.n}=\Pi_{[-C_q,C_q]}\widehat q_{p.n}}
Q_{P,1-p.\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_{p.n};\bar g_{p.n},\bar q_{p.n})-\theta_0(P)\right|\right),
\]
where \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) denotes the sample-size-\(p.n\) specialization of the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), and the infimum is over measurable estimators on the finite sample space \((O_1,\ldots,O_{p.n})\).

a9167a224585589403d31878148994186a6e59d1.title: Treatment-innovation transform \(M\)
a9167a224585589403d31878148994186a6e59d1.body:
Define the treatment-innovation moment-generating function by
\[
M(z)=E_P\!\left[e^{z\eta}\right].
\]
Given a zero \(z_0\) of \(M\) with multiplicity \(\ell\), define
\[
J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}.
\]

f23d4bedc00d9ad1f86563035f90c21334652bd4.title: Local Gaussian Benchmarks
f23d4bedc00d9ad1f86563035f90c21334652bd4.body:
Let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a positive nonincreasing real sequence with \(\delta_n\to0\), and fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\in\mathbb R\).  The following two assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple with \(p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta}\), \(p.C_g=C_g\), \(p.C_q=C_q\), \(p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}\), \(p.k=4\), and \(p.r=3\).  For any \(a\in(0,1]\) and any model \(m\), assume that the treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has law
\[
\eta\sim \sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Assume also \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}, and assume the treatment-code \(L^1\) radius condition at sample size \(n=p.n\).  Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path benchmark conclusion holds for \(p,m,a\) with constant \(C\).

\item \textbf{(Local ACE oracle envelope.)} For every published ACE handle, every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and every \(C_{\gamma}\in\mathbb R\), if the handle satisfies the JMS ACE theorem-five-four conclusion at \((\gamma,C_{\gamma})\), then \(C_{\gamma}>0\) and the following local ACE statement holds.  For every parameter tuple \(p\) with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), if
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}>0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\varepsilon_{2,n}>0,
\]
where \(n=p.n\), then for every deterministic treatment code \(gcode\), deterministic outcome code \(qcode\), and model \(m\), whenever
\[
\bar g_n=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}gcode_n
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\bar q_n=\Pi_{[-C_q,C_q]}qcode_n,
\]
the law belongs to the local JMS ACE class at threshold \(\delta_n\), and the local JMS eligibility condition at threshold \(\delta_n\) holds, the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator obeys
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}
\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\mathrm{jmsBound}(p,n,C_{\gamma},\delta_n).
\]
Moreover, for all real numbers \(risk,U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), if \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{DML}}\) and \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), then
\[
risk\le \min\{U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

328a59b67e3aa11f19d8eb64390a23521f4687bb.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
328a59b67e3aa11f19d8eb64390a23521f4687bb.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have primitive constants \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment-wide primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and whose supplied radius sequences are the common functions \(\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon_2\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and define its clipped pair by
\[
\bar g_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g(p)\},C_g(p)\},
\qquad
\bar q_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q(p)\},C_q(p)\}.
\]
Write \(n_j=p_j.n\). Suppose \(n_j\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\{m:\ m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j)\text{ of }\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class},\ 
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
where \(\bar G_{p,m,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{g^m_n(x),-C_g(p)\},C_g(p)\}\) and
\(\bar Q_{p,m,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{q^m_n(x),-C_q(p)\},C_q(p)\}\). Suppose also that, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
n_j\ge 2,
\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_g(p_j)R_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1},
\]
with \(R_1(p)=R_0(p)+1\). Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\) the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
Moreover, the same statistic satisfies
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j)\\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\ 
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}}}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(m)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian fixed-code class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p)\) in \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) satisfies
\[
\theta_0(m)=0.
\]
For every parameter value \(p\) and every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if
\[
\{m:\ m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p),\
\bar G_{p,m,p.n}=\bar g_{p,p.n},\
\bar Q_{p,m,p.n}=\bar q_{p,p.n}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

ef81c02e8e9e7dc1dff6eac0aabb864ab3fe702f.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
ef81c02e8e9e7dc1dff6eac0aabb864ab3fe702f.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold. Write \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}(p)\) for the parameter-record specialization of the non-Gaussian class in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), and write \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p)\) for the parameter-record specialization of the Gaussian class in \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\). For a model \(m\) with deterministic code sequences \(g^m\) and \(q^m\), set
\[
\bar G_{p,m,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{g^m_n(x),-C_g(p)\},C_g(p)\},
\qquad
\bar Q_{p,m,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{q^m_n(x),-C_q(p)\},C_q(p)\}.
\]

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have primitive constants \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment-wide primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and whose supplied radius sequences are common functions \(\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon_2\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and define
\[
\bar g_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g(p)\},C_g(p)\},
\qquad
\bar q_{p,n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q(p)\},C_q(p)\}.
\]
Write \(n_j=p_j.n\). Suppose \(n_j\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\{m:\ m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j),\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
\[
n_j\ge 2,
\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_g(p_j)R_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1(p)=R_0(p)+1\). Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\),
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
For the same sufficiently large \(j\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}(p_j)\\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}}}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(m)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian fixed-code class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p)\) satisfies
\[
\theta_0(m)=0.
\]
For every parameter value \(p\) and every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if
\[
\{m:\ m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p),\
\bar G_{p,m,p.n}=\bar g_{p,p.n},\
\bar Q_{p,m,p.n}=\bar q_{p,p.n}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
then
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

25894d7e9b5595a89d7e98cfe9e1999c37a16fb9.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
25894d7e9b5595a89d7e98cfe9e1999c37a16fb9.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) be any parameter record whose values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) are the fixed values above, and fix experiment-wide primitive bank and range records as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and whose radius sequences are the common functions \(\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon_2\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair. Write \(n_j=p_j.n\), and set
\[
\bar g_{p_j,n_j}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_{n_j}(x),-C_g(p_j)\},C_g(p_j)\},
\qquad
\bar q_{p_j,n_j}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_{n_j}(x),-C_q(p_j)\},C_q(p_j)\}.
\]
For a model \(m\), write
\[
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}(x)=\min\{\max\{g^m_{n_j}(x),-C_g(p_j)\},C_g(p_j)\},
\qquad
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}(x)=\min\{\max\{q^m_{n_j}(x),-C_q(p_j)\},C_q(p_j)\}.
\]
Suppose \(n_j\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\{m:\ m\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\text{ at }(p_j,n_j),\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}\}\neq\varnothing,
\]
\[
n_j\ge 2,
\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_g(p_j)R_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1(p)=R_0(p)+1\). Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and the fixed primitive bank record, for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank record for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), and
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
For the same sufficiently large \(j\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\sup_{\substack{m\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\text{ at }(p_j,n_j)\\
\bar G_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar g_{p_j,n_j},\
\bar Q_{p_j,m,n_j}=\bar q_{p_j,n_j}}}
\mathbb E_m\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(m)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.

\item \textbf{(Gaussian fixed-code class.)} For every parameter record \(p\) and every model \(m\), if \(m\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at \((p,p.n)\), then
\[
\theta_0(m)=0.
\]
For every parameter record \(p\) and every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), set
\[
\bar g_{p,p.n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_{p.n}(x),-C_g(p)\},C_g(p)\},
\qquad
\bar q_{p,p.n}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_{p.n}(x),-C_q(p)\},C_q(p)\}.
\]
If
\[
\{m:\ m\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\text{ at }(p,p.n),\
\bar G_{p,m,p.n}=\bar g_{p,p.n},\
\bar Q_{p,m,p.n}=\bar q_{p,p.n}\}\neq\varnothing,

then
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]

2c8e52af0afd98dd210f95e871e111314c17640a.title: Common Experiment Rates
2c8e52af0afd98dd210f95e871e111314c17640a.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have fixed values \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix the primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same fixed values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and with supplied radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1\) and \(\varepsilon_2\) equal to the corresponding radius sequences in every \(p_j\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and let its clipped coordinates at \(p_j\) be
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat g_{n_j}(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat q_{n_j}(x),-C_q\},C_q\},
\]
where \(n_j=p_j.n\). Suppose that \(n_j\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\), there is a model in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) at \((p_j,n_j)\) whose clipped supplied treatment and outcome codes equal the two clipped coordinates above,
\[
n_j\ge 2,
\qquad
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_gR_1(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, writing \(B\) for the translated-dyadic contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\) the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and the minimax risk over this fixed-code Non-Gaussian class satisfies
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\mathfrak R_{n_j}^{\mathrm{NG}}
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
Moreover, the same statistic witnesses the upper bound:
\[
\sup
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j},
\]
where the supremum ranges over the models in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) at \((p_j,n_j)\) with the fixed clipped supplied treatment and outcome codes displayed above.

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model in the Gaussian class of \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) at sample size \(p.n\) satisfies
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), whenever the corresponding clipped-code Gaussian intersection is nonempty, the Gaussian minimax risk and Gaussian quantile risk satisfy
\[
\mathfrak R_{p.n}^{\mathrm G}=0,
\qquad
\mathfrak M_{p.n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

ec07c89a2db98329973c1a99aade8a4fb8fdc218.title: Local and Gaussian Benchmarks
ec07c89a2db98329973c1a99aade8a4fb8fdc218.body:
Let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a positive nonincreasing real sequence with \(\delta_n\to0\).  Fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\in\mathbb R\).  The following assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following statement holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple satisfying
\[
p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad
p.C_g=C_g,\qquad
p.C_q=C_q,\qquad
p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\qquad
p.k=4,\qquad
p.r=3 .
\]
For any \(a\in(0,1]\) and any model \(m\), suppose that the treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has law
\[
\eta\sim \sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Suppose also that the i.i.d. product law is used at sample size \(n\), that \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian} hold, and that the treatment-code radius condition holds at sample size \(n\).  Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path benchmark conclusion holds for \(p,m,a\) with constant \(C\).

\]

\]

\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}
\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le

\]

\[

\]

c1aff3762b21b915912cce9048bc1fc50ba41498.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
c1aff3762b21b915912cce9048bc1fc50ba41498.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) have primitive constants
\(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment-wide primitive records \((\mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star})\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence sharing these primitive constants with \(p_0\), and sharing deterministic radius sequences \((\varepsilon_{1,n})\) and \((\varepsilon_{2,n})\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair. For each \(p\) and \(n\), write the corresponding fixed-code non-Gaussian class as the set of laws \(P\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} at \((p,n)\) whose clipped model codes agree at index \(n\) with
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Suppose \(n_j=p_j.n\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}\neq\varnothing,\qquad
2\le n_j,\qquad
\varepsilon_{1,n_j}\le
\bigl(4R_1(p_j)\exp\{2C_gR_1(p_j)\}\bigr)^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1(p)=R_0(p)+1\) is the search radius. Then there exist constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is delivered by the represented execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\frac{c}{n_j}\le
\mathfrak R_{n_j}^{\mathrm{NG}}
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]
The same statistic satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n_j}}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n_j}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every law \(P\) in the Gaussian class of \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at sample size \(p.n\) satisfies
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), whenever the clipped-code Gaussian intersection at \((p,p.n)\) is nonempty,
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

4ba53aade618a538bc1f2949af359747903ba3a3.title: ACE Spectral Alignment
4ba53aade618a538bc1f2949af359747903ba3a3.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Fix a published order-\(r\) ACE handle with estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\).  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}\) be the corresponding published JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad
p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(g_{\mathrm{code}},q_{\mathrm{code}}\), the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\) implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(p.s=p.r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} For every model \(P\), if the supplied codes satisfy the common clipped-code convention
\[
\bar G_{p,n,P}=\mathrm{clip}_{p,n}(g_{\mathrm{code}}),
\qquad
\bar Q_{p,n,P}=\mathrm{clip}_{p,n}(q_{\mathrm{code}}),
\]
\(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose that the supplied clipped codes admit at least one model in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), that \(n\ge2\), that \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and that
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}},
\]
where the supremum is over models satisfying the same common clipped-code convention.

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) and supplied code sequences \(g_{\mathrm{code}},q_{\mathrm{code}}\), assume that, for every \(n\ge1\),
\[
p_n.n=n,\quad p_n
\text{ has the same fixed experiment constants as }p_0,\quad
p_n.\varepsilon_{1,\cdot}=p_0.\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\quad
p_n.\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}=p_0.\varepsilon_{2,\cdot},\quad
p_n.\gamma=\gamma.
\]
Assume also that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\),
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_n)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_n))\}^{-1},
\]
and the supplied clipped codes admit at least one model in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

e9c9e6ff39e46898ed8658bb1c63511d1a15bc02.title: Local Gaussian Benchmarks
e9c9e6ff39e46898ed8658bb1c63511d1a15bc02.body:
Let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a positive nonincreasing real sequence with \(\delta_n\to0\), and fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\in\mathbb R\).  The following assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} There is a constant \(C>0\), depending on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following statement holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple with
\[
p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad
p.C_g=C_g,\qquad
p.C_q=C_q,\qquad
p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\qquad
p.k=4,\qquad
p.r=3 .
\]
For any \(a\in(0,1]\) and any model \(m\), suppose that the treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has law
\[
\eta\sim \sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Suppose also that \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}\) hold and that the treatment-code radius condition holds at sample size \(p.n\).  Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path benchmark conclusion holds for \(p,m,a\) with constant \(C\).

\item \textbf{(Local ACE oracle envelope.)} For every published ACE handle, every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and every \(C_{\gamma}\in\mathbb R\), if the handle satisfies the JMS ACE theorem-five-four conclusion at \((\gamma,C_{\gamma})\), then \(C_{\gamma}>0\) and the following local ACE statement holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\) and with
\[
\varepsilon_{1,p.n}>0,\qquad \varepsilon_{2,p.n}>0 .
\]
For any deterministic treatment-code sequence \(g_{\mathrm{code}}\), deterministic outcome-code sequence \(q_{\mathrm{code}}\), and model \(m\), suppose that the clipped supplied regressions at sample size \(p.n\) are generated by \(g_{\mathrm{code}}\) and \(q_{\mathrm{code}}\).  If the law belongs to the local JMS ACE class at threshold \(\delta_{p.n}\) and the local JMS eligibility condition holds at threshold \(\delta_{p.n}\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}
\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,p.n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\operatorname{jmsBound}(p,p.n,C_{\gamma},\delta_{p.n}).
\]
Moreover, for all real numbers \(risk,U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), if \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{DML}}\) and \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), then
\[
risk\le \min\{U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

5356ab7d0ff673129cb36ff68f64a12ef8c1cd96.title: Minimax quantile risk $\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}$
5356ab7d0ff673129cb36ff68f64a12ef8c1cd96.body:
At \(n=p.n\), define
\[
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\ 
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\ 
\bar g_n=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}\widehat g_n,\ 
\bar q_n=\Pi_{[-C_q,C_q]}\widehat q_n}
Q_{P,1-p.\gamma}\!\left(
\left|
\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)-\theta_0(P)
\right|
\right).
\]
Here \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is evaluated at the sample size \(n=p.n\), and the infimum ranges over measurable estimators on the finite sample space \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\).

p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(g_{\mathrm{code}},q_{\mathrm{code}}\), write
\[
\bar G_{p,n,P}=\mathrm{clip}_{p,n}\bigl(g_{\mathrm{code}}(n,\cdot)\bigr),
\qquad
\bar Q_{p,n,P}=\mathrm{clip}_{p,n}\bigl(q_{\mathrm{code}}(n,\cdot)\bigr)
\]
for the common clipped-code convention at \(n=p.n\).  Also write
\(\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)=R_1(p)\) for the outer search radius determined by \(p\).  Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(p.s=p.r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} For every model \(P\), if the common clipped-code convention above holds, \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose that the supplied clipped codes admit at least one model in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), that \(n\ge2\), that \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, that \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and that
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}},
\]
where the supremum is over models satisfying the same common clipped-code convention.

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) and supplied code sequences \(g_{\mathrm{code}},q_{\mathrm{code}}\), assume that, for every \(n\ge1\),
\[
p_n.n=n,\quad p_n
\text{ has the same fixed experiment constants as }p_0,\quad
p_n.\varepsilon_{1,\cdot}=p_0.\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\quad
p_n.\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}=p_0.\varepsilon_{2,\cdot},\quad
p_n.\gamma=\gamma.
\]
Assume also that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\),
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_n)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_n))\}^{-1},
\]
and the supplied clipped codes admit at least one model in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

2d827d559f3ecc81cbe4d5707c145d68b73fa8f8.title: Fixed-code law class \(\mathcal L\)
2d827d559f3ecc81cbe4d5707c145d68b73fa8f8.body:
For a class \(\mathcal P_n\), an index \(n\), and a base law \(P_{\mathrm{base}}\), the fixed-code law class is
\[
 \mathcal L
 =
 \{P\in\mathcal P_n:\ 
   \bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(P_{\mathrm{base}}),\
   \bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(P_{\mathrm{base}})\}.
\]
Here \(\bar g_n(P)\) is the law-indexed clipped supplied treatment code under \(P\), and \(\bar q_n(P)\) is the corresponding law-indexed clipped supplied outcome code.

ea712203ec5bd1cb999a22b221155d4f75990896.title: Contour-bank handle \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\)
ea712203ec5bd1cb999a22b221155d4f75990896.body:
Let \(\operatorname{Name}(x)\) denote a supplied certified-real record for \(x\), and let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote such a record together with a rational positivity witness. As part of the experiment convention, fix once for all the single actual record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k,\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k\) is exact and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1),
\]
with value contracts
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and it is the primitive record used by both the bank and the estimator. The construction reads exactly its supplied interval, modulus, and positivity fields.

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one. If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), put
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1.
\]
For \(q=0,\ldots,2^{m_{\star}-1}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record \(\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}})\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_q
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
Its value is \(\rho_q=R_0+1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\). Enumerate these radii increasingly and set
\[
 C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}.
\]

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),
\]
\[
 u_{\star}=2e_{\star}
 +N_{\mathrm{cert}}(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}>0.
\]
Every output datum is obtained by the displayed finite modulus calls, rational endpoint operations, and primitive recursion over displayed integer bounds. The admissible operations are precisely these bounded certified-record operations, and reusing the identical fixed record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) gives the same bank and certificate for every \(n\).

eb48a1c2713d9d28b55ace4913d16f3609c0de7a.title: Certified contour-bank handle $\mathfrak p_{\star}$
eb48a1c2713d9d28b55ace4913d16f3609c0de7a.body:
Let \(\operatorname{Name}(x)\) denote an actually supplied certified-real record for the real number \(x\), and let \(\operatorname{Name}_{+}(x)\) denote such a record together with a rational positive lower-bound witness. As part of the experiment convention, fix once and for all the supplied record
\[
 \mathfrak p_{\star}=
 \bigl(k,\mathfrak d_{\star},\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star},
       \mathfrak r_{0,\star},\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\bigr),
\]
where \(k\) is exact and
\[
 \mathfrak d_{\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\delta),\quad
 \mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(\psi_{\eta}),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{0,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_0),\quad
 \mathfrak r_{1,\star}:\operatorname{Name}_{+}(R_1).
\]
The value contracts are
\[
 k=r+1,\qquad
 R_0=(2^{k+4}k!)^{1/(k-2)}
       (\psi_{\eta}^2/\delta)^{1/(k-2)},
 \qquad R_1=R_0+1.
\]
Each positive name includes its rational positivity witness. The record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) is fixed before \(n\), the law, or the sample varies, and it is the single primitive record used by both the bank and the estimator. The construction is determined solely by the supplied interval, modulus, and positivity fields of this record, with quantification over the fixed supplied records representing the displayed constants.

Invoke the supplied moduli of \(\mathfrak p_{\eta,\star}\) and \(\mathfrak r_{1,\star}\) at error one. If the returned intervals have rational upper endpoints \(u_{\psi}\) and \(u_R\), define
\[
 U_{\psi}=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_{\psi}\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 U_R=\left\lceil\max\{1,u_R\}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3.
\]
Set
\[
 m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,
 \qquad d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},
 \qquad h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,
 \qquad J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1.
\]
For each \(q=0,\ldots,2^{m_{\star}-1}\), use certified addition on the fixed record \(\mathfrak r_{0,\star}\) and the rational point record for \(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}\) to form
\[
 \mathfrak\rho_q
 =\mathfrak r_{0,\star}+\operatorname{Name}(1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}).
\]
Its value is
\[
 \rho_q=R_0+1/4+q2^{-m_{\star}}.
\]
Enumerate these radii increasingly and set
\[
 C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}.
\]

Define the integers
\[
 e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,
 \qquad
 d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),
\]
\[
 u_{\star}=2e_{\star}
 +N_{\mathrm{cert}}(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}),
 \qquad
 a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}}>0.
\]
Every output datum is obtained by the displayed finite modulus calls, rational endpoint operations, and primitive recursion over the displayed integer bounds. The construction is a finite certified procedure in the supplied records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), and reuse of this identical record gives the same bank and certificate for every \(n\).

9d3edcefd626cb848a01aac6e263a68849784037.title: Local Gaussian Benchmarks
9d3edcefd626cb848a01aac6e263a68849784037.body:
Let \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a positive nonincreasing real sequence with \(\delta_n\to0\).  Fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\in\mathbb R\).  The following two assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be any admissible parameter tuple with \(p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta}\), \(p.C_g=C_g\), \(p.C_q=C_q\), \(p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}\), \(p.k=4\), and \(p.r=3\).  For any \(a\in(0,1]\) and any model \(m\), suppose
\[
\eta\sim \sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).  Assume \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}, and assume the treatment-code radius condition at sample size \(p.n\).  Then the Gaussian--Rademacher path conclusion holds for \(p,m,a\) with constant \(C\).

\item \textbf{(Local ACE oracle envelope.)} For every published ACE handle, every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), and every \(C_{\gamma}\in\mathbb R\), if the handle satisfies the JMS ACE theorem-five-four conclusion at \((\gamma,C_{\gamma})\), then \(C_{\gamma}>0\) and the following local ACE statement holds.  For every admissible parameter tuple \(p\) with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), if \(\varepsilon_{1,p.n}>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,p.n}>0\), then for every deterministic treatment code \(gcode\), deterministic outcome code \(qcode\), and model \(m\), whenever
\[
\bar g_{p.n}=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}gcode_{p.n},
\qquad
\bar q_{p.n}=\Pi_{[-C_q,C_q]}qcode_{p.n},
\]
the law belongs to the local JMS ACE class at threshold \(\delta_{p.n}\), and the local JMS eligibility condition at threshold \(\delta_{p.n}\) holds, equivalently the same eligibility object \(\mathsf E_{p.n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with the fixed threshold \(\delta\) replaced by \(\delta_{p.n}\), one has
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}
\!\left(\left|
\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},p.r,p.n}(gcode,qcode)-\theta_0(P)
\right|\right)
\le
\mathrm{jmsBound}(p,p.n,C_{\gamma},\delta_{p.n}).
\]
Moreover, for all real numbers \(risk,U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), if \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{DML}}\) and \(risk\le U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\), then
\[
risk\le \min\{U_{\mathrm{DML}},U_{\mathrm{ACE}}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

27121347c4938b9959dba1a4fcd2b92b6d908bd3.title: External treatment code \(\widehat g_n\)
27121347c4938b9959dba1a4fcd2b92b6d908bd3.body:
We say that \(\widehat g_n\) is the external treatment code at sample size \(n\) when \(\widehat g_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is a fixed deterministic measurable covariate map, chosen before the inference sample is drawn, with established clipped version
\[
\bar g_n=\Pi_{[-C_g,C_g]}\circ\widehat g_n .
\]

ce455e31a2c711f7eb1d5e1dd7b004925480a0de.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
ce455e31a2c711f7eb1d5e1dd7b004925480a0de.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}>0\). For every measurable covariate space, the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) be any parameter value with fixed primitive constants \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\). Let \((p_j)_{j\ge1}\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and with supplied radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2\) equal to the corresponding radius fields of every \(p_j\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, and let \((\bar g_n,\bar q_n)\) be the code pair clipped at \([-C_g,C_g]\) and \([-C_q,C_q]\), respectively. Suppose \(n_j=p_j.n\to\infty\) and, for all sufficiently large \(j\), the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item the class of models satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) at \((p_j,n_j)\) and having clipped codes \((\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\) is nonempty;
\item \(n_j\ge 2\);
\item
\[
\varepsilon_1(n_j)\le
\Bigl(4\,\operatorname{searchRadius}(p_j)
\exp\{2C_g\,\operatorname{searchRadius}(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\) is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by the corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n_j}\right)
\le
\operatorname{minimaxRisk}(p_j,n_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right).
\]
Moreover, the same statistic witnesses the upper bound:
\[
\sup_{P}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right),
\]
where the supremum ranges over all models satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) at \((p_j,n_j)\) with clipped codes \((\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\).

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model in \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) at \((p,p.n)\) satisfies \(\theta_0(P)=0\). For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), whenever the clipped-code intersection of \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) at \((p,p.n)\) is nonempty,
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{minimaxQuantileRiskG}(p,p.n;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

8070d1e144c82bf924b7be3a00c5fac4bde4541f.title: ACE--Spectral Alignment
8070d1e144c82bf924b7be3a00c5fac4bde4541f.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) be the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator carried by a fixed published ACE handle.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under the common clipped-code convention, the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(s=r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} If \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds, and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

95bacae9c095b6b155d1cd45da21b1849db6998b.title: ACE Spectral Alignment
95bacae9c095b6b155d1cd45da21b1849db6998b.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) be the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator carried by a fixed published ACE handle.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under the common clipped-code convention, the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(s=r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} If \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds, and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

ab3ac523a23cec4b88d13a93a5e5b55a27f64c7d.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
ab3ac523a23cec4b88d13a93a5e5b55a27f64c7d.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}>0\). For every measurable covariate space, the following two assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) be any parameter value with primitive constants \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment-wide primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and whose two radius fields are the fixed deterministic sequences \(n\mapsto \varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(n\mapsto \varepsilon_{2,n}\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, with clipped versions
\[
\bar g_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
\bar q_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Writing \(n_j=p_j.n\) and \(R(p)=R_0(p)+1\) for the search radius, suppose that \(n_j\to\infty\) and that, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\begin{itemize}
\item the class of models satisfying \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} at \((p_j,n_j)\) and having clipped codes \((\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\) is nonempty;
\item \(n_j\ge 2\);
\item
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n_j}\le
\Bigl(4R(p_j)\exp\{2C_gR(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by its corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n_j}\right)
\le
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{NG}}_{n_j}(p_j;\widehat g,\widehat q)
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right).
\]
Moreover, the same statistic satisfies
\[
\sup_{P}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right),
\]
where the supremum ranges over all models satisfying \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} at \((p_j,n_j)\) with clipped codes \((\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\).

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at \((p,p.n)\) has \(\theta_0(P)=0\). For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if the clipped-code subclass satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at \((p,p.n)\) is nonempty, then
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm G}_{n}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0,
\qquad
\mathfrak M^{\mathrm G}_{n,1-\gamma}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

f139ca507abdf11c7d7f31f1b9932ed7b1d0eb87.title: Fixed-code Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)\) and risk \(\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}\)
f139ca507abdf11c7d7f31f1b9932ed7b1d0eb87.body:
For supplied nuisance-code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_n)_{n\ge 1}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_n)_{n\ge 1}\), with clipped sequences \(\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}=(\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}_n)_{n\ge 1}\) and \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}=(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}_n)_{n\ge 1}\), define the fixed-code Gaussian-intersection class by
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:
g_P^{\mathrm{clip}}=\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}
\ \text{and}\
q_P^{\mathrm{clip}}=\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}
\right\}.
\]
The corresponding minimax risk is
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(n;\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\!\left[
\left(
\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\theta_0(P)
\right)^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum ranges over measurable estimators
\(\widetilde\theta:\mathcal O^n\to\mathbb R\).

f574947be71c9e6191c2af07fef2a2634c9b9ded.title: Clipped outcome code \(\bar Q_n\)
f574947be71c9e6191c2af07fef2a2634c9b9ded.body:
We say \(\bar Q_n\) is the clipped supplied outcome-code function at sample size \(n\) when, for every covariate value \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
\bar Q_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]

ed3f31147be371bd52f775c981b314680e0d3bd8.title: Clipped treatment-code sequence \(\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}\)
ed3f31147be371bd52f775c981b314680e0d3bd8.body:
We say \(\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}=(\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}_n)_{n\ge 1}\) is the clipped treatment-code sequence when, for each sample size \(n\) and covariate value \(x\),
\[
\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\}.
\]

aa5c9e852827196f7bdbbd79467a44fd0679903d.title: Clipped outcome-code sequence \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}\)
aa5c9e852827196f7bdbbd79467a44fd0679903d.body:
We say \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}=(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}_n)_{n\ge 1}\) is the clipped supplied outcome-code sequence when, for each sample size \(n\), \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}_n\) is the covariate map obtained by projecting \(\widehat q_n\) onto \([-C_q,C_q]\): for every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}_n(x)=\min\{C_q,\max\{-C_q,\widehat q_n(x)\}\}.
\]

3791c8e7c73e77d4516d1eb6452df58e658af913.title: ACE Spectral Alignment
3791c8e7c73e77d4516d1eb6452df58e658af913.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\) and constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) satisfying
\[
2\le r,\qquad
0<\delta,\quad 0<C_{\theta},\quad 0<C_g,\quad 0<C_q,\quad
0<\psi_{\eta},\quad 0<\psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that the following holds on any measurable covariate space.  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) be the published order-\(r\) ACE estimator carried by a fixed published ACE handle.  For every \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the corresponding JMS constant.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple with
\[
p_0.r=r,\quad p_0.\delta=\delta,\quad p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad p_0.C_g=C_g,\quad p_0.C_q=C_q,\quad p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\quad p_0.\gamma=\gamma,
\]
and fix one experiment-wide certified contour-bank and range record for \(p_0\).  For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and with \(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied treatment and outcome code sequences \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under the common clipped-code convention, the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class inclusion.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class} implies membership in the non-Gaussian spectral class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(ACE comparison subclass.)} For every model \(P\), membership in the ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} implies membership in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).  If \(s=r\), then these two classes coincide at \(n=p.n\).

\item \textbf{(Published ACE upper guarantee.)} If \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), the JMS eligibility condition of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds at sample index \(n=p.n\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\Big[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+
64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
