\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\Big].
\]

\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} Suppose \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), the JMS eligibility condition of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds at sample index \(n=p.n\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1}.
\]
Then the adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, built from the fixed certified records transported from \(p_0\) to \(p\), satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Upper-guarantee comparison.)} For any triangular parameter sequence \(p_n\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\), and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), assume that eventually \(n\ge2\), the JMS eligibility condition of \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility} holds at sample index \(n=p_n.n\), \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), the displayed spectral small-radius condition holds, and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is nonempty for the supplied clipped codes.  If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+
C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{
\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
}{
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
}
\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

2b1a72cdab0adf701c24a83116277760a2e52ce9.title: Fixed-code Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)\)
2b1a72cdab0adf701c24a83116277760a2e52ce9.body:
For supplied nuisance-code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_n)_{n\ge 1}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_n)_{n\ge 1}\), with sample-index clipped maps \(\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}_n\) and \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}_n\), define
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:
g_P^{\mathrm{clip}}=\widehat g^{\mathrm{clip}}_n
\ \text{and}\
q_P^{\mathrm{clip}}=\widehat q^{\mathrm{clip}}_n
\right\}.
\]
The corresponding minimax risk is
\[
\operatorname{minimaxRiskG}(n;\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(\widehat g,\widehat q)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\!\left[
\left(
\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\theta_0(P)
\right)^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum ranges over measurable estimators
\(\widetilde\theta:\mathcal O^n\to\mathbb R\).

c6ba238d47aa44bdf648e76a068b3c347065ed80.title: Common Experiment Dichotomy
c6ba238d47aa44bdf648e76a068b3c347065ed80.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}>0\). For every measurable covariate space, the following two assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian sequence.)} Let \(p_0\) be any parameter value with primitive constants \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and fix experiment-wide primitive records \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) and \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle,obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \((p_j)\) be any parameter sequence with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\), and whose two radius fields are the fixed deterministic sequences \(n\mapsto\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(n\mapsto\varepsilon_{2,n}\). Let \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\) be any measurable deterministic code pair, with clipped versions
\[
\bar g_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
\bar q_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Writing \(n_j=p_j.n\) and \(R(p)=R_0(p)+1\), suppose that \(n_j\to\infty\) and that, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\begin{itemize}
\item the subclass of models satisfying \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} at \((p_j,n_j)\) and having clipped codes \((\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\) is nonempty;
\item \(n_j\ge 2\);
\item
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n_j}\le
\Bigl(4R(p_j)\exp\{2C_gR(p_j)\}\Bigr)^{-1}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then there are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, with \(B\) the contour bank generated from \(p_0\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), for all sufficiently large \(j\), the transported primitive bank for \(p_j\) generates the same bank \(B\), the statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator} is measurable, every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and compilation specification is represented by its corresponding execution on the transported primitive records, and
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{c}{n_j}\right)
\le
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{NG}}_{n_j}
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right),
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{NG}}_{n_j}\) denotes the minimax mean-squared risk over the subclass satisfying \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} at \((p_j,n_j)\) with clipped codes \((\bar g_{n_j},\bar q_{n_j})\). Moreover, the same statistic satisfies
\[
\sup_{P}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n_j}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\operatorname{ofReal}\!\left(\frac{C}{n_j}\right),
\]
where the supremum ranges over that same clipped-code non-Gaussian subclass.

\item \textbf{(Gaussian class.)} For every parameter value \(p\), every model satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at \((p,p.n)\) has \(\theta_0(P)=0\). For every measurable deterministic code pair \((\widehat g_n,\widehat q_n)\), if the subclass satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} at \((p,p.n)\) with clipped codes \((\bar g_{p.n},\bar q_{p.n})\) is nonempty, then
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm G}_{p.n}=0,
\qquad
\mathfrak M^{\mathrm G}_{p.n,1-\gamma}=0.
\]
Here \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm G}_{p.n}\) and \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm G}_{p.n,1-\gamma}\) are the Gaussian minimax mean-squared risk and Gaussian minimax \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile risk for this clipped-code subclass.
\end{itemize}

fb67915c996c9935bc1d163e7771e584a37de8be.title: Observable transform factorization
fb67915c996c9935bc1d163e7771e584a37de8be.body:
Suppose \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as specified in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).  For \(z\in\mathbb C\), write
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{zZ_n}],\qquad
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}],\qquad
H_n(z)=E_P[e^{zD_n}],
\]
where \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), and \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\).  Also write
\[
G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}],\qquad
B_n(z)=E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n}],
\]
where \(b_n(X)\) is the outcome-contamination term entering the residual transform.  Then, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)
\]
and
\[
G_n(z)=\theta_0 F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]

c91320e9057f76be2ddf11ce3a733a61d0922e11.title: Exact contour identification
c91320e9057f76be2ddf11ce3a733a61d0922e11.body:
Fix \(n\ge 1\), a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), and a certified contour-bank input \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}\). For any bank index \(j\in\{0,\ldots,J\}\), let \(C_j\) be the positively oriented circle with radius \(\rho_j\), and let
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{zZ_n}],\qquad
G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}],\qquad
H_n(z)=E_P[e^{z\{g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\}}].
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Residual zero-freeness.)} \(F_n(z)\ne 0\) for every \(z\in C_j\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance zero-freeness.)} \(H_n(z)\ne 0\) for every \(z\) on or inside \(C_j\).
\item \textbf{(Positive contour count.)} The zero count \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\), counted with multiplicity inside \(C_j\), satisfies \(N_{C_j}(F_n)\ge 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then the contour functional of \(\cref{obj:def:contour-functional}\) identifies the partially linear coefficient and is given by the normalized contour integral:
\[
(\theta_0(P):\mathbb C)
=
\Theta_{C_j}(F_n,G_n)
=
\{N_{C_j}(F_n)\,2\pi i\}^{-1}
\oint_{C_j}\frac{G_n(z)}{F_n(z)}\,dz .
\]

cfedef665e62761de2208621282672f2172f64f0.title: Known zero instrument
cfedef665e62761de2208621282672f2172f64f0.body:
Fix \(n\ge 1\) and a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Let
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}],
\qquad
Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X),
\qquad
H_n(z)=E_P[e^{z\{g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\}}].
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(\ell\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Zero.)} \(z_0\in\mathbb C\) satisfies \(M(z_0)=0\).
\item \textbf{(Multiplicity.)} The analytic order of \(M\) at \(z_0\) is \(\ell\).
\end{itemize}
For the zero-based instrument \(J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:zero-instrument}\), the following identities hold:
\[
\forall d\in\mathbb R,\qquad E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0,
\]
\[
E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0
\qquad P\text{-a.s.},
\]
and
\[
E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\ne 0\),
\[
\theta_0
=
\frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
{E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]

4cf2992e1ba6ad95013c178ef76d0127f488563f.title: Finite contour bank
4cf2992e1ba6ad95013c178ef76d0127f488563f.body:
Fix the primitive parameter record \(p\), the positive certified-real input record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}\), an index \(n\) with \(n\ge 1\), and a law \(P\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) as specified by \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Let \(B\) be the contour-bank data computed from \((p,\mathfrak p_{\star})\), with constants \(U_{\psi},U_R,N_{\mathrm{cert}},m_{\star},d_{\star},h_{\star},e_{\star},d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}},u_{\star},a_{\star}\), total size \(J\), and radii \(\rho_j\).

Then the following properties hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive certificate.)} \(a_{\star}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Bookkeeping identities.)}
\[
\begin{gathered}
N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^2(U_R+2)^3,\qquad
m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,\qquad
J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1,\\
d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad
h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,\qquad
e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^2(U_R+1)^2,\\
d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),\qquad
u_{\star}=2e_{\star}+N_{\mathrm{cert}}\bigl(m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}\bigr),\qquad
a_{\star}=2^{-u_{\star}} .
\end{gathered}
\]
\item \textbf{(Bank geometry.)} The radii are strictly increasing and satisfy
\[
R_0<\rho_j<R_1
\]
for every bank index \(j\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform treatment-noise certificate.)} For the treatment-noise moment-generating function \(M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]\), there is a bank index \(j\) such that, with \(C_j=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=\rho_j\}\),
\[
N_{C_j}(M)\ge 1
\]
and
\[
a_{\star}\le |M(z)|\qquad\text{for every }z\in C_j .
\]
\end{itemize}

3ce76fc753bcbba177f1e32a31c2a3d043f1c6dc.title: Hard submodel lower bound
3ce76fc753bcbba177f1e32a31c2a3d043f1c6dc.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}>0\), with \(\tau\le \psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds for every parameter tuple whose displayed constants are \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and every \(n\ge 1\).

If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) is nonempty, then there are a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Preserved observed margins and codes.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has the same law of \((X,T)\) as \(P^{\circ}\), the same \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), and the same clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome representation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
holds \(P_{n,\vartheta}\)-almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Local relative entropy.)} For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\), if \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}

Moreover, for every starting law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\), there is a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(ACE-class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Preserved observed margins and nuisance quantities.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0\), \(q_0\), treatment innovation \(\eta\), and clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\circ}\), and satisfies the treatment-code and outcome-code radius conditions appearing in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome representation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
holds \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)-almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Local relative entropy.)} For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\), if \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}

Finally, for every pair of clipped-code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n=\bar q\), then
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g,\bar q)}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\ \bar g_n=\bar g,\ \bar q_n=\bar q}}
E_P\!\left[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2\right].
\]

4a530d210fc8fdf9597372a874395ab24d5bb5c3.title: Symmetric mixture reduction
4a530d210fc8fdf9597372a874395ab24d5bb5c3.body:
For any real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), there is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on these four constants, such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be a parameter configuration with \(p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta}\), \(p.C_g=C_g\), \(p.C_q=C_q\), and \(p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}\), and let \(P\) be a law in the corresponding model with sample size \(n=p.n\).  Assume the usual measurability and integrability conditions, and suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are drawn according to the i.i.d. product law in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).
\item \textbf{(Symmetric mixture.)} The treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has law
\[
\tfrac12 N(-1,1)+\tfrac12 N(1,1).
\]
\item \textbf{(Independence and ranges.)} The treatment innovation is independent of \(X\) as in \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise}\), the outcome innovation satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence}\), and the range and tail conditions in \(\cref{obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}\) hold.
\item \textbf{(Treatment code.)} The supplied treatment code obeys
\[
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{1,n},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le \frac1\pi .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the fourth cumulant of \(\eta\) is
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=-2,
\]
the treatment-innovation moment-generating function \(M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]\) satisfies
\[
M(i\pi/2)=0,
\]
and, writing \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) and \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\),
\[
E_P\!\left[
Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)
\right]
=
e^{-\pi^2/8}
E_P\!\left[
\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n}{2}\right)
\right],
\]
with
\[
\frac{e^{-\pi^2/8}}{2}
\le
E_P\!\left[
Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)
\right].
\]
Moreover, for the sine estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:sine-estimator}\),
\[
E_P\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n}.
\]

267dff181d3b1576ae357717eb2b5e9223a0d9b1.title: Uniform transform concentration
267dff181d3b1576ae357717eb2b5e9223a0d9b1.body:
Fix \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},R_1\in\mathbb R\). There is a constant \(K>0\), depending on these displayed constants, such that the following holds. Let \(p\) be a parameter tuple and let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) be represented by a model in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Primitive constants.)} The primitive constants of \(p\) are \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and its search radius is \(R_1\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) follow the i.i.d. product law specified in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).
\item \textbf{(Fold.)} \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and the corresponding inference fold \(I_a\) is nonempty.
\end{itemize}
With \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), define
\[
\widehat F_{a,n}(z)=\frac{1}{|I_a|}\sum_{i\in I_a}\exp(zZ_{n,i}),
\qquad
\widehat G_{a,n}(z)=\frac{1}{|I_a|}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_i\exp(zZ_{n,i}),
\]
and
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[\exp(zZ_n)],
\qquad
G_n(z)=E_P[Y\exp(zZ_n)].
\]
Then
\[
E\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}\left|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)\right|^2\right]
+
E\!\left[\sup_{|z|\le R_1}\left|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)\right|^2\right]
\le \frac{K}{|I_a|}.
\]

05c56cb4de5c89570ef68563ee2324f9aae2412b.title: ACE and spectral alignment
05c56cb4de5c89570ef68563ee2324f9aae2412b.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants
\[
\delta,\ C_{\theta},\ C_g,\ C_q,\ \psi_{\eta},\ \psi_{\xi}.
\]
There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending on these fixed constants, such that the following statements hold. Let \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the published JMS generalized-quantile constant at level \(\gamma\), and fix a published order-\(r\) ACE estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\). Let \(p_0\) be a parameter tuple whose primitive constants are \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) and whose probability level is \(\gamma\). Fix one certified contour-bank record and one certified range record for \(p_0\). For any parameter tuple \(p\) with the same values of \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) as \(p_0\) and probability level \(\gamma\), and for any supplied clipped treatment and outcome codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class relations.)} Every law in the published ACE class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) belongs to the non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Every law in the ACE-comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\). If \(s=r\), then \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).
\item \textbf{(ACE upper guarantee.)} For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) whose treatment and outcome codes are the supplied clipped codes, if the eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge 0\), then
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where
\[
B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
=
C_{\gamma}r!16^r\delta^{-1}
\left[
\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
+64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
\{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
(\gamma n)^{-1/2}
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{(Spectral upper guarantee.)} If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) contains a law whose treatment and outcome codes are the supplied clipped codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds, \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\left\{4R(p)\exp(2C_gR(p))\right\}^{-1},
\]
where \(R(p)\) is the search radius used by the adaptive contour estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), then the estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) constructed from the fixed certified records satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\right|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Asymptotic comparison.)} For any sequence \(p_n\) with sample size \(n\), the same fixed constants as \(p_0\), the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\) as \(p_0\), and probability level \(\gamma\), suppose that for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
n\ge2,\qquad
\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}},\qquad
\varepsilon_{1,n}>0,\qquad
\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0,\qquad
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\left\{4R(p_n)\exp(2C_gR(p_n))\right\}^{-1},
\]
and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) contains a law whose treatment and outcome codes are the supplied clipped codes. If
\[
\frac{\varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
+C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}}
{n^{-1/2}}
\to\infty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{\sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}}{B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}}
\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

62bb04bb4c15c3d9f131cbec92424f669d6e3c4b.title: Gaussian class degeneracy
62bb04bb4c15c3d9f131cbec92424f669d6e3c4b.body:
Fix any parameter tuple with positive sample size \(n\), integers \(r\) and \(k\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge 2\), an exponent \(s\ge r\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) on positive indices. On any measurable covariate space, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degenerate target.)} For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\), the partially linear coefficient obeys
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero minimax risks.)} For any supplied code sequences \(g_n\) and \(q_n\), if \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) contains a law whose clipped treatment and outcome codes agree pointwise at index \(n\) with
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\},
\]
then
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

9643bc88908e6c1d036937e170701e54cdab6caf.title: Adaptive root-n minimax
9643bc88908e6c1d036937e170701e54cdab6caf.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\).  There exist constants
\(c,C>0\), depending only on these displayed constants, with the following
property.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameter records.)} Let \(p_0\) be any primitive parameter record
whose fixed entries are
\[
p_0.r=r,\qquad
p_0.\delta=\delta,\qquad
p_0.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad
p_0.C_g=C_g,\qquad
p_0.C_q=C_q,\qquad
p_0.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\qquad
p_0.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}.
\]
Let \(p\) be any primitive parameter record with the same seven fixed entries
as \(p_0\).  Thus \(p\) carries its own sample size \(n=p.n\ge 1\), cumulant
order \(k=p.r+1\), comparison exponent \(s\ge p.r\), probability level
\(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), positive Gaussian scale, and nonnegative nonincreasing
code-radius sequences.

\item \textbf{(Shared fixed records.)} Work on any measurable covariate space and
fix one pair of experiment-wide primitive records for \(p_0\).  The contour
bank and range records used at \(p\) are the transports of this same pair along
the equality of the seven fixed entries.

\item \textbf{(Base supplied codes.)} Let \(P^{\mathrm{base}}\) be any model under
\(p\).  The statistic is the total Borel statistic
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of
\(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), formed with the transported fixed
records and the supplied treatment code \(\bar g_n\) of \(P^{\mathrm{base}}\).
\end{itemize}

Then \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is measurable.  Moreover, every
compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build and
compilation contract for these transported fixed records and this supplied
treatment code realizes the represented execution of the same statistic.

For every model \(P\), membership in the JMS ACE class of
\(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) implies membership in the non-Gaussian class of
\(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).  If \(s=r\), then membership in the JMS ACE
class is equivalent to membership in the ACE comparison subclass of
\(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\).

Assume now that the i.i.d. sampling condition of \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\)
holds for \(P^{\mathrm{base}}\), that the non-Gaussian class with the same
supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\mathrm{base}}\) is nonempty, that
\(n\ge 2\), and that
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}
\le
\{4R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\}^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1\) is the search radius in \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\)
at the transported fixed constants.  Then
\[
\frac{c}{n}
\le
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
\le
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(P^{\mathrm{base}}),\,
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(P^{\mathrm{base}})}}
E_P\!\left[
  \{\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\}^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(P^{\mathrm{base}}),\,
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(P^{\mathrm{base}})}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(
  |\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|
\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}}.
\]

Finally, if the JMS ACE class with the same supplied codes
\(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\mathrm{base}}\) is nonempty, \(n\ge 2\), and the
same treatment-code threshold holds, then
\[
\frac{c}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(P^{\mathrm{base}}),\,
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(P^{\mathrm{base}})}}
E_P\!\left[
  \{\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\}^2
\right]
\le
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(P^{\mathrm{base}}),\,
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(P^{\mathrm{base}})}}
E_P\!\left[
  \{\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)\}^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\\
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(P^{\mathrm{base}}),\,
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(P^{\mathrm{base}})}}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(
  |\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|
\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}}.
\]

718246443a771ec319e7812c2db1b485c24a468f.title: ACE class relations
718246443a771ec319e7812c2db1b485c24a468f.body:
Fix a parameter tuple \(p\) with ACE order \(r\), comparison exponent \(s\), cumulant order \(k=r+1\), \(2\le r\), \(r\le s\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \((\varepsilon_{1,n})\) and \((\varepsilon_{2,n})\) on positive indices. For every class index \(n\) and every law \(P\) with its supplied regression codes satisfying the usual measurability and integrability conditions,
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
\]
where the two classes are those of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) and \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Moreover,
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}},
\]
where \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) is the subclass in \(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\). If \(s=r\), then for every such \(P\),
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]

a692f67712b66ba4bacd6254be6438600ef15fb8.title: Gaussian--Rademacher sine benchmark
a692f67712b66ba4bacd6254be6438600ef15fb8.body:
Fix real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\).  There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on these four constants, such that the following statement holds.  Let \(p\) be an admissible parameter tuple satisfying
\[
p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad p.C_g=C_g,\qquad p.C_q=C_q,\qquad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},\qquad k=4,
\]
let \(a\in(0,1]\), and let \(P\) be a law in the model \(m\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} The treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has the law of
\[
\eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\) and \(S\) are independent.
\item \textbf{(Sampling and model restrictions.)} The law satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}\).
\item \textbf{(Current treatment-code radius.)} For the clipped supplied treatment code \(\bar g_n\),
\[
\int |\,\bar g_n(x)-g_0(x)\,|\,dP_X(x)\le \varepsilon_{1,n},
\]
under the usual integrability condition for this \(L^1(P_X)\) quantity.
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},\qquad
A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},\qquad
\Delta_a=2a^4.
\]
Then the treatment-innovation moment-generating function satisfies
\[
M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
\]
the fourth cumulant satisfies \(\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4\), and \(t_a>0\) is the first positive zero of the characteristic transform: \(M_a(it_a)=0\) and \(M_a(iu)\ne0\) for every \(u\in(0,t_a)\).  Moreover, for every \(d\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P[\sin\{t_a(\eta+d)\}]=0.
\]

Let \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) and \(D_n=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\).  If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/2\), then
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]
=A_aE_P[\cos(t_aD_n)]
\]
and
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/2.
\]
With \(\mathbb P_n\) denoting empirical averaging over \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,n}
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
 \frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
      {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
 &\displaystyle \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
 0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
\]
where \(\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}\) clips to \([-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]\).  Its mean squared risk obeys
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n a^{-2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
The same smallness condition also gives
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le \frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi}
\]
and the equivalent cumulant-parameterized bound
\[
 E_P[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2]
 \le
 C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\}.
\]

11adce4ace6a5e9f6b66a22d1f31674d68388ec8.title: I.i.d. sampling
11adce4ace6a5e9f6b66a22d1f31674d68388ec8.body:
The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P\):
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P.
\]

37d943d9903c56451a4e381f60c746edc69514ee.title: Independent treatment innovation
37d943d9903c56451a4e381f60c746edc69514ee.body:
The treatment innovation \(\eta\) is independent of the covariate \(X\):
\[
\eta\perp X.
\]

00914e30b9d12389a93d47010350549f8ba29b60.title: Outcome mean independence
00914e30b9d12389a93d47010350549f8ba29b60.body:
The outcome innovation \(\xi\) satisfies
\[
E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0
\]
almost surely.

10d6a35228dcbceea501edc1fb81e1ac8996e737.title: Coefficient range
10d6a35228dcbceea501edc1fb81e1ac8996e737.body:
The partially linear coefficient \(\theta_0\) satisfies
\[
|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}.
\]

091e1f69fe2f8b8a3786bbef2c39560b3bda2697.title: Bounded Gaussian outcome
091e1f69fe2f8b8a3786bbef2c39560b3bda2697.body:
The outcome coordinate \(Y\) satisfies
\[
|Y|\le C_q
\]
almost surely.

a2edc03298b76f735ed8ec2eaaa271fad0d73725.title: Treatment innovation tail
a2edc03298b76f735ed8ec2eaaa271fad0d73725.body:
With the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian norm convention
\[
\lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
=
\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le2\},
\]
the treatment innovation \(\eta\) satisfies
\[
\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}.
\]

a0beac192ced3d4a9eaf9fe59c3e826416d2657e.title: Outcome innovation tail
a0beac192ced3d4a9eaf9fe59c3e826416d2657e.body:
The outcome innovation \(\xi\) satisfies
\[
\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}
\]
almost surely.

b85b9fc3bbe28fe47c34a2296ba8eee8deb703fc.title: Cumulant separation
b85b9fc3bbe28fe47c34a2296ba8eee8deb703fc.body:
For the cumulant order \(k\), the treatment innovation \(\eta\) satisfies
\[
|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta.
\]

c21a5c1354cf1a354a6179c8097617e3e4c0eaf6.title: Treatment code radius
c21a5c1354cf1a354a6179c8097617e3e4c0eaf6.body:
For every \(n\), the supplied treatment code \(\bar g_n\) satisfies
\[
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]

4e141e9bf094163a8973628c16c7b77833bbfa99.title: Outcome code radius
4e141e9bf094163a8973628c16c7b77833bbfa99.body:
For every \(n\), the supplied outcome code \(\bar q_n\) satisfies
\[
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]

240017f43583ebfecbfd091c8ede9bdf2514883d.title: Non-Gaussian law class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\)
240017f43583ebfecbfd091c8ede9bdf2514883d.body:
For an observed-data law \(P\) on \(O=(X,T,Y)\), define
\[
g_0(x)=E_P[T\mid X=x],
\qquad
q_0(x)=E_P[Y\mid X=x],
\]
let \(\theta_0(P)\) be the constant coefficient in the partially linear conditional mean
\[
E_P[Y\mid X,T]=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\{T-g_0(X)\},
\]
and set
\[
\eta=T-g_0(X),
\qquad
\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)\eta.
\]
Given \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation}\), the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) consists of all such laws \(P\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment innovation.)} \(\eta\perp X\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome mean.)} \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient range.)} \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Nuisance ranges.)} \(\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g\) and \(\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Innovation tails.)} \(\|\eta\|_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(\|\xi\|_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code control.)} \(\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome code.)} The supplied outcome code \(\bar q_n\) is unrestricted in the definition of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).
\end{itemize}

fbd3f5e67fc161924f9bd185c92b8dc734728b93.title: JMS eligibility \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)

507f6d4cc922407cfdcd76f493a66e1ebcdfe540.title: ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)
507f6d4cc922407cfdcd76f493a66e1ebcdfe540.body:
Relative to \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), define
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
\quad
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) is the subclass of the broad spectral class that satisfies both supplied-code restrictions.

b2430405843a7712d326dfba444e7527c24c604e.title: Certified contour arithmetic substrate \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\)
b2430405843a7712d326dfba444e7527c24c604e.body:
The paper-independent bounded-build obligation \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) is the following finite implementation specification. A certified real record consists of rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic contract
\[
x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
\qquad
I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e.
\]
A positive record additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) such that \(p\le x\). Executable code is restricted to inspecting the interval, modulus, and positivity fields.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
\qquad
A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
and
\[
AB=
\left[
\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
\max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}
\right].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\). Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are implemented by these endpoint operations and
\[
(A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), set
\[
\operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
\begin{cases}
0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
\min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
\operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Then \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by the rational interval obtained by adding the corresponding square bounds. Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures: after \(q\) bisections their width is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\). This supplies certified modulus lower and upper bounds. Division is the guarded operation
\[
\frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
=
(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
executed when the modulus routine has returned a rational lower bound \(m>0\); outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\) is then sound.

The certified name of \(\pi\) is constructed from Machin's identity
\[
\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\), the first \(N+1\) terms of
\[
\arctan x=\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}+R_N(x),
\qquad
|R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3},
\]
give rational nested enclosures after intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested enclosures. If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the explicit choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\), giving an effective modulus with finite fuel.

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations. The Lagrange remainders are bounded respectively by
\[
3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
\qquad
\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
\qquad
\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\); since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this displayed \(N\) gives a sound error at most \(e\). Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested. Hence
\[
\exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle. Combining the constructed \(\pi\) name with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius record \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\) and \(0\le q<N\), certified circle-node records for
\[
r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
\quad\text{and}\quad
2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive. If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), a uniform mesh with
\[
N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell. Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the displayed finite number of operations therefore yields sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures. Their fuel consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and a finite number of endpoint operations. Absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) exactly when it implements these algorithms, exports their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiles the resulting module. This definition records the explicit bounded-build obligation. Later executable conclusions are conditional on a compiled build satisfying this specification.

2c221f6980d09d408df158bc85629af07a438e7f.title: Local-to-Gaussian frontier
2c221f6980d09d408df158bc85629af07a438e7f.body: For triangular treatment-noise laws with \(|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n\) and \(\delta_n\downarrow0\) under the same supplied code sequences, a natural next question is whether there exists a data-driven selector among ordinary DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour procedures that attains the sharp minimax mean-squared-error rate as a function of \((n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n)\), yields uniformly valid inference across these regimes, and admits a matching local minimax lower bound. Resolving this question requires specifying a sharp-rate functional, a uniform-inference or coverage criterion, an existential selector, a confidence procedure, and a matching lower-bound witness.

60336bad2ab81fcc6a1dc85ed10075fc2409259e.title: Observable transform factorization
60336bad2ab81fcc6a1dc85ed10075fc2409259e.body:
Let \(n\ge 1\), and let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfy \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}. Put
\[
Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X),\qquad
D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X),
\]
and let \(b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0D_n(X)\), as in \cref{obj:def:outcome-contamination}. Define, for \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{zZ_n}],\quad
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}],\quad
H_n(z)=E_P[e^{zD_n(X)}],
\]
and
\[
G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}],\qquad
B_n(z)=E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n(X)}].
\]
Then, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)
\]
and
\[
G_n(z)=\theta_0 F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]

90608e3e5601e3900c66be047daaf06d36204d4d.title: Zero-based instrument identity
90608e3e5601e3900c66be047daaf06d36204d4d.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfy \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) for an index \(n\ge 1\). Let
\[
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}],\qquad Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X),\qquad D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X),
\]
and write \(H_n(z)=E_P[e^{zD_n(X)}]\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Multiplicity.)} \(\ell\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Zero.)} \(z_0\in\mathbb C\) satisfies \(M(z_0)=0\).
\item \textbf{(Analytic order.)} The analytic order of \(M\) at \(z_0\) is \(\ell\).
\end{itemize}
For the zero-based instrument \(J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}e^{z_0w}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:zero-instrument}\), the following identities hold:
\[
\forall d\in\mathbb R,\qquad E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)]=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
E_P[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X]=0
\quad P\text{-a.s.},
\]
and
\[
E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]
=
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\ne 0\),
\[
\theta_0(P)
=
\frac{E_P[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}
{E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]}.
\]

f1324b2b5c033a1fcc511ea76e98d2ef29275cb6.title: Symmetric mixture reduction
f1324b2b5c033a1fcc511ea76e98d2ef29275cb6.body:
Fix real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\).  There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on these four constants, such that the following holds for every parameter tuple whose corresponding entries are \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), every sample size \(n\) in that tuple, and every law \(P\) on \(O=(X,T,Y)\).

Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are sampled according to the i.i.d. product law in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).
\item \textbf{(Symmetric mixture noise.)} The treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has law
\[
\frac12 N(-1,1)+\frac12 N(1,1).
\]
\item \textbf{(Independence and mean restrictions.)} The law \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence}\).
\item \textbf{(Range and tail bounds.)} The law \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}\) with constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code radius.)} For \(D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\), the supplied treatment code obeys its \(L^1(P_X)\) radius at the sample size \(n\), and \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/\pi\).
\end{itemize}
Then the fourth cumulant and the imaginary-axis moment-generating function value are
\[
\kappa_4(\eta)=-2,
\qquad
M(i\pi/2)=0.
\]
Moreover, for \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\),
\[
E_P\!\left[
Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)
\right]
=
e^{-\pi^2/8}
E_P\!\left[
\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi D_n(X)}{2}\right)
\right],
\]
and this common denominator is bounded below as
\[
\frac{e^{-\pi^2/8}}{2}
\le
E_P\!\left[
Z_n\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi Z_n}{2}\right)
\right].
\]
For the clipped sine-ratio estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:sine-estimator}\),
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\bigl(\widehat\theta_{\sin,n}-\theta_0(P)\bigr)^2
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n}.
\]

93664984b23335ded626a50b724089419c7e455f.title: ACE and spectral alignment
93664984b23335ded626a50b724089419c7e455f.body:
Fix an ACE order \(r\ge2\) and positive constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\).  There is a constant
\(C_{\mathrm{spec}}>0\), depending only on these fixed constants, such that
the following statements hold.

Let \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), let \(C_{\gamma}>0\) be the constant in the
published order-\(r\) ACE generalized-quantile guarantee, and write
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}\) for the estimator supplied by that
published ACE handle.  Let \(p_0\) be a parameter record whose
\(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(\gamma\)
coordinates equal the displayed constants, and fix the certified primitive
bank and range records associated with \(p_0\).  For any parameter record
\(p\) sharing the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\) and satisfying
\(p.\gamma=\gamma\), and for any supplied code sequences whose clipped
versions are \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\), the following hold, under the
usual measurability and integrability conditions.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Class relations.} For every \(n=p.n\),
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
If \(p.s=r\), then the common clipped-code convention gives
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]
Here the classes and the comparison subclass are those of
\(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class,obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\).

\item \textbf{ACE upper guarantee.} If a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)
uses the clipped supplied treatment and outcome codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\),
if the JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of
\(\cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility,obj:def:jms-eligibility-quantities}\) holds,
and if \(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\), then
\[
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \bigl(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{ACE},r,n}-\theta_0(P)|\bigr)
 \le B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma},
\]
where \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}\) is the generalized quantile in
\(\cref{obj:def:generalized-quantile}\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
 &= C_{\gamma} r!16^r\delta^{-1}
 \Big[
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   + C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}  \\
 &\qquad\qquad
   +64(C_g+\psi_{\eta})^r
   \{r^2(C_g+\psi_{\eta})+\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta}\}
   (\gamma n)^{-1/2}
 \Big].
\end{aligned}
\]

\item \textbf{Spectral upper guarantee.} If
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) contains at least one law using
the clipped supplied codes, \(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds,
\(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), and
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}
 \le
 \{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p)\exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p))\}^{-1},
\]
then the certified contour statistic
\(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) of
\(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), built from the fixed primitive
records, satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}}
 Q_{P,1-\gamma}
 \bigl(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|\bigr)
 \le
 \sqrt{\frac{C_{\mathrm{spec}}}{\gamma n}},
\]
where the supremum ranges over laws in the published ACE class whose clipped
supplied treatment and outcome codes are \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\).

\item \textbf{Upper-guarantee separation along sequences.} For any sequence
\((p_n)\) with \(p_n.n=n\), the same fixed experiment constants as \(p_0\),
the same radius sequences \(\varepsilon_{1,\cdot},\varepsilon_{2,\cdot}\),
and \(p_n.\gamma=\gamma\), suppose that eventually
\(n\ge2\), \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) holds,
\(\varepsilon_{1,n}>0\), \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\ge0\),
\[
 \varepsilon_{1,n}
 \le
 \{4\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_n)
 \exp(2C_g\,\mathrm{searchRadius}(p_n))\}^{-1},
\]
and the published ACE class contains a law using the clipped supplied codes.
If
\[
 \frac{
   \varepsilon_{1,n}^r\varepsilon_{2,n}
   + C_{\theta}\varepsilon_{1,n}^{r+1}
 }{n^{-1/2}}
 \longrightarrow \infty,
\]
then
\[
 \frac{
   \sqrt{C_{\mathrm{spec}}/(\gamma n)}
 }{
   B_{\mathrm{ACE},n,\gamma}
 }
 \longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}

b01fabcf557a057305d3d42c2c308361c67ee6ed.title: Gaussian--Rademacher sine benchmark
b01fabcf557a057305d3d42c2c308361c67ee6ed.body:
For any real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\xi}\), there is a constant \(C>0\) such that the following statement holds.  Let \(p\) be any parameter tuple with \(p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta}\), \(p.C_g=C_g\), \(p.C_q=C_q\), \(p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi}\), and \(p.k=4\).  Let \(a\in(0,1]\), where \(a\) is the Gaussian--Rademacher mixing parameter, and let \(P\) be any law in the model indexed by \(p\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gaussian--Rademacher path.)} The treatment innovation \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\) has law
\[
\eta_a=\sqrt{1-a^2}\,G_{\circ}+aS,
\]
where \(G_{\circ}\sim N(0,1)\), \(S\) is symmetric Rademacher, and \(G_{\circ}\perp S\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling and structural conditions.)} The law satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian}\), under the usual measurability and integrability conditions.
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code radius.)} At the current sample size \(n=p.n\),
\[
\int |\,\bar g_n(x)-g_0(x)\,|\,dP_X(x)\le \varepsilon_{1,n},
\]
with the corresponding absolute error integrable.
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
t_a=\frac{\pi}{2a},
\qquad
A_a=a\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{8a^2}\right\},
\qquad
\Delta_a=2a^4.
\]
Then the treatment-innovation moment-generating function and fourth cumulant satisfy
\[
M_a(z)=\exp\!\left(\frac{1-a^2}{2}z^2\right)\cosh(az),
\qquad
\kappa_4(\eta_a)=-2a^4.
\]
Moreover, \(t_a>0\), \(M_a(i t_a)=0\), \(M_a(iu)\ne0\) for every \(u\in(0,t_a)\), and
\[
E_P[\sin\{t_a(\eta+d)\}]=0
\]
for every real \(d\).  If \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/2\), then, with \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\) and \(D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\),
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]
=
A_aE_P[\cos\{t_aD_n(X)\}]
\]
and
\[
E_P[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/2.
\]
For the estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_{a,n}
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}
\frac{\mathbb P_n[Y\sin(t_aZ_n)]}
     {\mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]},
&\displaystyle \mathbb P_n[Z_n\sin(t_aZ_n)]\ge A_a/4,\\[3mm]
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
the same condition \(t_a\varepsilon_{1,n}\le 1/2\) gives
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2\right]
\le
C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n a^{-2}
\exp\!\left(\frac{(1-a^2)\pi^2}{4a^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
It also implies
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\frac{\Delta_a^{1/4}}{2^{1/4}\pi}
\]
and the equivalent cumulant-scale bound
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0)^2\right]
\le
C\min\!\left\{1,\frac1n\Delta_a^{-1/2}
\exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)\right\}.
\]

98dbf140b9671f1b9903ee721793e953a02342fd.title: Adaptive root-n minimaxity
98dbf140b9671f1b9903ee721793e953a02342fd.body:
Fix \(r\ge 2\) and positive constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\).  Then there are constants \(c>0\) and \(C>0\), depending only on these fixed primitive constants, such that the following statements hold.

For every measurable covariate space, let \(p_0\) be a parameter record whose primitive entries \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) equal the fixed constants above, and fix one experiment-wide record consisting of the certified contour-bank input and the represented range input for \(p_0\).  For every parameter record \(p\) with the same primitive entries as \(p_0\), and for every base model satisfying the usual measurability, conditional-mean, and integrability requirements, set \(n=p.n\).  Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) be the total Borel statistic of \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), constructed from the transported fixed records and the base treatment-code sequence.  Define the fixed-code non-Gaussian class
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}(p;\mathrm{base})
=
\{P:\ P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\text{ of }\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class},\ 
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(\mathrm{base}),\ 
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(\mathrm{base})\}.
\]
Define the fixed-code JMS ACE class
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})
=
\{P:\ P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\text{ of }\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class},\ 
\bar g_n(P)=\bar g_n(\mathrm{base}),\ 
\bar q_n(P)=\bar q_n(\mathrm{base})\}.
\]

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Measurable statistic.)}  The statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is measurable.
\item \textbf{(Represented execution.)}  For every compiled bounded spectral adapter satisfying the full canonical build-and-compilation specification for \(p\), the transported fixed records, and the base treatment-code sequence, the represented-data execution realizes the same \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\).
\item \textbf{(Class relations.)}  Every law in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\).  If \(s=r\), then \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) coincides with the \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\).
\item \textbf{(Non-Gaussian fixed-code risk.)}  If the sample law is the i.i.d. product law of \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}(p;\mathrm{base})\) is nonempty, \(n\ge 2\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le \{4R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\}^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1\) is the search radius from the contour-bank construction in \(\cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}\), then
\[
\frac{c}{n}
\le
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}(p;\mathrm{base})}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}(p;\mathrm{base})}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}},
\]
with generalized lower quantiles as in \(\cref{obj:def:generalized-quantile}\).
\item \textbf{(ACE fixed-code risk.)}  If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})\) is nonempty, \(n\ge 2\), and
\[
\varepsilon_{1,n}\le \{4R_1\exp(2C_gR_1)\}^{-1},
\]
then
\[
\frac{c}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})}
E_P\!\left[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\]
where the infimum is over measurable real-valued estimators of \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).  Moreover,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}(p;\mathrm{base})}
Q_{P,1-\gamma}\!\left(|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\theta_0(P)|\right)
\le
\sqrt{\frac{C}{\gamma n}}.
\]
\end{itemize}

5f4c4d6453c057369cb05a5300f2f5e957e33cc5.title: Generalized quantile \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\)
5f4c4d6453c057369cb05a5300f2f5e957e33cc5.body:
With the sampling structure in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, let \(P\) be an observed-data law, let \(n\ge 1\), and let \(W=W(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) be a real-valued sample statistic. Under \(P^{\otimes n}\), write
\[
F_W(t)=\Pr(W\le t)
\]
for the distribution function of \(W\). For \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), the generalized lower \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile of \(W\) is
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)
=
\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F_W(t)\ge 1-\gamma\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\) is the left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F_W\) evaluated at level \(1-\gamma\).

c213230477a9e0c96ead868f8a8e9bee0d9c6823.title: Treatment-code error \(D_n\) and contamination \(b_n\)
c213230477a9e0c96ead868f8a8e9bee0d9c6823.body:
In the law class specified by \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, fix a law \(P\), an index \(n\), and the clipped supplied treatment code \(\bar g_n\). The treatment-code error \(D_n\) and the outcome contamination \(b_n\) are the covariate functions
\[
D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X),
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0\{g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\}=q_0(X)-\theta_0D_n(X).
\]

7c5c2e05066640bb37b1c04bcb718451a47006c5.title: JMS quantities \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\)
7c5c2e05066640bb37b1c04bcb718451a47006c5.body:
Under \cref{obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation,obj:ass:jms-treatment-code-radius,obj:ass:jms-outcome-code-radius}, the four quantities entering the Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis order-\(r\) eligibility condition at index \(n\) are
\[
a_{1,n}=2\log\!\left(\frac{6(C_g+\psi_{\eta})}{\varepsilon_{1,n}}\right),
\qquad
b_{1,n}=\log\!\left(\frac{\gamma n}{9}\right),
\qquad
a_2=4(C_g+\psi_{\eta}),
\]
and
\[
b_{2,n}
=
\frac{200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\,\delta}
{\max\bigl\{\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \varepsilon_{2,n},\ (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\bigr\}}.
\]

347b3dbcdaf132dce415622b636d88770dc9600f.title: JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)
347b3dbcdaf132dce415622b636d88770dc9600f.body:
Let \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\) be the quantities in \cref{obj:def:jms-eligibility-quantities}. For every index \(n\) for which the following expressions are defined, \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) is the condition
\[
r
\le
\min\left\{
\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}-\frac{1}{a_{1,n}}\log\!\left(\frac{b_{1,n}}{a_{1,n}}\right),
\frac{b_{2,n}}{a_2\log(a_2b_{2,n})}
\right\}.
\]

22ca0972e10a03624f284cc346d8eddb6aaf18a6.title: I.i.d. sampling
22ca0972e10a03624f284cc346d8eddb6aaf18a6.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the observations satisfy
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P .
\]

d25e4d395f509eb3bd1c994222c559ec43fda656.title: Independent treatment noise
d25e4d395f509eb3bd1c994222c559ec43fda656.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the treatment innovation is independent of the covariates:
\[
\eta \perp X .
\]

9fe72d0f5a7da351b161e8346588e52685e4d4a2.title: Outcome mean independence
9fe72d0f5a7da351b161e8346588e52685e4d4a2.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the outcome innovation has conditional mean zero given the covariates and treatment:
\[
E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0
\]
almost surely.

4e9219342845e30b8f030f6c2463d225da0c45b3.title: Coefficient range
4e9219342845e30b8f030f6c2463d225da0c45b3.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the partially linear coefficient satisfies
\[
|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}.
\]

54531efedf5db97b570b3e21b670bdcd0fb73e2e.title: Treatment regression range
54531efedf5db97b570b3e21b670bdcd0fb73e2e.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the treatment regression satisfies
\[
\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g.
\]

9f561df74f613bab245ef6ae60488c7f5cb14f36.title: Outcome regression range
9f561df74f613bab245ef6ae60488c7f5cb14f36.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the outcome regression satisfies
\[
\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q.
\]

d067374dcf3329ffed9e9bfab09d47353506506a.title: Bounded outcome
d067374dcf3329ffed9e9bfab09d47353506506a.body:
In the model of \cref{obj:def:plm-model} with constants as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, the outcome is uniformly bounded:
\[
|Y|\le C_q
\]
almost surely.

f6328bbc7914d451657109ca005cc9b5da807320.title: Sub-Gaussian treatment noise
f6328bbc7914d451657109ca005cc9b5da807320.body:
In the model of \cref{obj:def:plm-model} with constants as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian norm is
\[
\lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
=
\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le 2\}.
\]
Under this convention, the treatment innovation satisfies
\[
\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le \psi_{\eta}.
\]

da4aa3f6739b266edf4e54be088c45ab5275c167.title: Sub-Gaussian outcome noise
da4aa3f6739b266edf4e54be088c45ab5275c167.body:
In the model of \cref{obj:def:plm-model} with constants as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, the outcome innovation satisfies
\[
\lVert \xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le \psi_{\xi}
\]
almost surely.

3062f14d8f54a4edf39cca0b4862c6f07d96de19.title: Cumulant separation
3062f14d8f54a4edf39cca0b4862c6f07d96de19.body:
In the model of \cref{obj:def:plm-model} with parameters as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, the \(k\)th cumulant of the treatment innovation satisfies
\[
|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge \delta.
\]

d9351502f453ed49e75b5d45060681cbfc1977d6.title: Treatment code radius
d9351502f453ed49e75b5d45060681cbfc1977d6.body:
In the model of \cref{obj:def:plm-model} with parameters as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\),
\[
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]

caa13037cdde8faa04891cd8b980e020fd35d423.title: Outcome code radius
caa13037cdde8faa04891cd8b980e020fd35d423.body:
In the model of \cref{obj:def:plm-model} with parameters as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\),
\[
\lVert \bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]

33215df8a0fd0fdb7c5e0c38f7c219b8303351eb.title: Treatment code radius
33215df8a0fd0fdb7c5e0c38f7c219b8303351eb.body:
In the notation of \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^r(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]

d181197d9e42f11726d9cb46558a2e51c994e7df.title: Outcome code radius
d181197d9e42f11726d9cb46558a2e51c994e7df.body:
In the notation of \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\lVert \bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^r(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]

9f7d722c878af1cf995330e3ad945ffe9172ad64.title: Gaussian treatment noise
9f7d722c878af1cf995330e3ad945ffe9172ad64.body:
In the notation of \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the treatment innovation satisfies
\[
\eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

2d39d888a020a44cd71d27b68e46daa0c34c5bf3.title: \(L^1\) treatment radius
2d39d888a020a44cd71d27b68e46daa0c34c5bf3.body:
In the notation of \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]

6f81ab0b18523f9cd9df77f8c5a5c8e4a390036c.title: Non-Gaussian law class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\)
6f81ab0b18523f9cd9df77f8c5a5c8e4a390036c.body:
In the notation of \cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation,obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \(O=(X,T,Y)\). Define
\[
g_0(x)=E_P[T\mid X=x],
\qquad
q_0(x)=E_P[Y\mid X=x],
\]
let \(\theta_0(P)\) be the constant coefficient in the partially linear conditional mean
\[
E_P[Y\mid X,T]=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\{T-g_0(X)\},
\]
and set
\[
\eta=T-g_0(X),
\qquad
\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)\eta.
\]
For each \(n\ge 1\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) is the class of such laws \(P\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Treatment independence.)} \(\eta\perp X\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome mean.)} \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient range.)} \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment regression range.)} \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome regression range.)} \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment tail.)} \(\lVert \eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le \psi_{\eta}\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome tail.)} \(\lVert \xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le \psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge \delta\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment code control.)} \(\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le \varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\end{itemize}

e1f22a8cfb9c5dd6abf9f1d7ff2f2819ee3bd844.title: Generalized quantile \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\)
e1f22a8cfb9c5dd6abf9f1d7ff2f2819ee3bd844.body:
In the sampling setting of \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, let \(P\) be an observed-data law, let \(n\ge 1\), and let \(W=W(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) be a real-valued statistic of the sample. Under \(P^{\otimes n}\), write
\[
F_W(t)=\Pr(W\le t)
\]
for the distribution function of \(W\). For \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), the generalized lower \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile of \(W\) is
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\ F_W(t)\ge 1-\gamma\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\) is the left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F_W\) evaluated at level \(1-\gamma\).

6fc2270f009f27be5ac3231c1776b11457736bbc.title: Treatment-code error \(D_n\) and contamination \(b_n\)
6fc2270f009f27be5ac3231c1776b11457736bbc.body:
With notation as in \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class,obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, fix a law \(P\), an index \(n\), and the clipped supplied treatment code \(\bar g_n\). The treatment-code error \(D_n\) and the induced outcome contamination \(b_n\) are the covariate functions
\[
D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X),
\qquad
b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0\{g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\}=q_0(X)-\theta_0D_n(X).
\]

bc73091d32c48de80a8c94a53493fcd686a3ae27.title: JMS eligibility quantities \(a_{1,n},b_{1,n},a_2,b_{2,n}\)
bc73091d32c48de80a8c94a53493fcd686a3ae27.body:
Under the notation and conditions in \cref{obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation,obj:ass:jms-treatment-code-radius,obj:ass:jms-outcome-code-radius,obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the four quantities entering the Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis order-\(r\) eligibility condition at index \(n\) are
\[
a_{1,n}=2\log\!\left(\frac{6(C_g+\psi_{\eta})}{\varepsilon_{1,n}}\right),
\qquad
b_{1,n}=\log\!\left(\frac{\gamma n}{9}\right),
\qquad
a_2=4(C_g+\psi_{\eta}),
\]
and
\[
b_{2,n}=
\frac{200\min\{1,C_{\theta}\}\,\delta}
{\max\bigl\{\varepsilon_{1,n},\ \varepsilon_{2,n},\ (\gamma n)^{-1/2}(\psi_{\xi}+C_{\theta}\psi_{\eta})\bigr\}}.
\]

958f7a6f8bc2f58686e111de4a687e68ad750cfd.title: Gaussian degeneracy and risk
958f7a6f8bc2f58686e111de4a687e68ad750cfd.body:
Fix any parameter tuple with sample size \(n\ge1\), integers \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge2\), an exponent \(s\ge r\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) that are nonnegative and nonincreasing on positive indices, with values \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\). On any measurable covariate space, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degenerate target.)} For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}, the partially linear coefficient obeys
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero minimax risks.)} For any deterministic supplied code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\), if there exists a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} whose clipped treatment and outcome codes agree pointwise at index \(n\) with
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\},
\]
then
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

062ea19a95c256ae71b66023f1aeda4abf252b8e.title: Non-Gaussian hard submodel
062ea19a95c256ae71b66023f1aeda4abf252b8e.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}>0\), with \(\tau\le \psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds for every parameter tuple whose displayed constants are \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and every \(n\ge 1\).

If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} is nonempty, then there are a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Preserved observed margins and codes.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has the same law of \((X,T)\) as \(P^{\circ}\), the same \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), and the same clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome representation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
holds \(P_{n,\vartheta}\)-almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Local relative entropy.)} For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\), if \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}

Moreover, for every starting law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}, there is a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(ACE-class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Preserved observed margins and nuisance quantities.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has the same law of \((X,T)\), the same \(g_0\), \(q_0\), treatment innovation \(\eta\), and clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\circ}\), and satisfies the treatment-code and outcome-code radius conditions in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome representation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
holds \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)-almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Local relative entropy.)} For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\), if \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}

Finally, for every pair of clipped-code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n=\bar q\), then
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g,\bar q)}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\ \bar g_n=\bar g,\ \bar q_n=\bar q}}
E_P\!\left[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2\right].
\]

314dbaa2aadaf2db5eb2c6f9d8f7ea3ee21bdec9.title: ACE class relations
314dbaa2aadaf2db5eb2c6f9d8f7ea3ee21bdec9.body:
Fix a parameter tuple \(p\) with ACE order \(r\), cumulant order \(k=r+1\), \(2\le r\), comparison exponent \(s\ge r\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \((\varepsilon_{1,n})\) and \((\varepsilon_{2,n})\) on positive indices. For every class index \(n\) and every model \(P\) with its supplied regression codes, under the usual measurability and integrability conditions,
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
\]
where the two classes are those of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class}. Moreover, for the \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) in \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass},
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}} .
\]
If \(s=r\), then for every such model \(P\),
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]

8a9418524f997bf22d4aa5c7a32474e83dc8cce4.title: ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)
8a9418524f997bf22d4aa5c7a32474e83dc8cce4.body:
Relative to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, define
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
\quad
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) is the subclass of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) satisfying the \(L^s(P_X)\) supplied-code restrictions for both \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\).

2b3308474d8bb1ae98c075e675a71a0b1f571374.title: ACE class relations
2b3308474d8bb1ae98c075e675a71a0b1f571374.body:
Fix a parameter tuple \(p\) with ACE order \(r\), cumulant order \(k=r+1\), \(2\le r\), comparison exponent \(s\) satisfying \(r\le s\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices. Fix any class index \(n\in\mathbb N\). Under the usual measurability and integrability conditions for laws \(P\) and their supplied regression codes, the following class relations hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(JMS ACE inclusion.)} For every law \(P\) with supplied codes,
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
\]
where the classes are those of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class}.
\item \textbf{(ACE comparison inclusion.)} For every law \(P\) with supplied codes,
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}},
\]
where \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) is the subclass in \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}.
\item \textbf{(Equal-exponent equivalence.)} If \(s=r\), then for every law \(P\) with supplied codes,
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]
\end{itemize}

81baaa790ac38bef44d197b0a53316d55066ac0f.title: Gaussian hard submodel
81baaa790ac38bef44d197b0a53316d55066ac0f.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants \(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants \(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}>0\), with \(\tau\le \psi_{\xi}\), such that the following holds for every admissible parameter tuple whose displayed constants are \(r,\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and every \(n\ge1\).

If \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class} is nonempty, then there are a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Preserved margin and codes.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has the same law of \((X,T)\) as \(P^{\circ}\), the same functions \(g_0\) and \(q_0\), and the same clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n\) and \(\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome representation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
holds \(P_{n,\vartheta}\)-almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Local relative entropy.)} For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\), if \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}

For every starting law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}, there is a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(ACE-class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Preserved margin and nuisance quantities.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has the same law of \((X,T)\), the same functions \(g_0,q_0\), the same treatment innovation \(\eta\), and the same clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) as \(P^{\circ}\), and it satisfies the treatment-code and outcome-code radius conditions in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome representation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
holds \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)-almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Local relative entropy.)} For all \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\in\mathbb R\), if \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and \(|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=h/\sqrt n\), then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}
