Finally, for every pair of clipped-code functions \(\bar g,\bar q:X\to\mathbb R\), if there exists a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n=\bar g\) and \(\bar q_n=\bar q\), then
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g,\bar q)}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\ \bar g_n=\bar g,\ \bar q_n=\bar q}}
E_P\!\left[(\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P))^2\right].
\]

dc36fd2bf823e90dde9e9b8ac78255e9c3ba1d8d.title: Gaussian square exponential bound
dc36fd2bf823e90dde9e9b8ac78255e9c3ba1d8d.body:
For every positive scale \(\psi>0\), let \(\zeta\sim N(0,(\psi/4)^2)\). Then \(\exp(\zeta^2/\psi^2)\) is integrable under the law of \(\zeta\), and
\[
\mathbb E\exp(\zeta^2/\psi^2)\le 2 .
\]

a70e8442b14b51b135ef91c93738fbd11e396813.title: Clipped ratio risk decomposition
a70e8442b14b51b135ef91c93738fbd11e396813.body:
Let \(n\ge1\), let \(W\) and \(R\) be real-valued functions on an observation space, and let \(\theta,C_{\theta},A,\mu_W\in\mathbb R\). Use the empirical-average notation of \(\cref{obj:def:model-parameters}\). Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Target range.)} \(|\theta|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(A>0\).
\item \textbf{(Mean denominator.)} \(A/2\le \mu_W\).
\end{itemize}
For any sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define \(\widehat\theta\) by
\[
\widehat\theta
=
\begin{cases}
\min\!\left\{\max\!\left\{\dfrac{\theta\,\mathbb P_n W+\mathbb P_n R}{\mathbb P_n W},-C_{\theta}\right\},C_{\theta}\right\},
& A/4\le \mathbb P_n W,\\
0, & A/4> \mathbb P_n W .
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
(\widehat\theta-\theta)^2
\le
\frac{16}{A^2}
\left\{
(\mathbb P_n R)^2
+
C_{\theta}^2\bigl(\mathbb P_n(W-\mu_W)\bigr)^2
\right\}.
\]

6a5a0e58029d56b0ffa195ab60b3d01403125b50.title: One-dimensional hard submodel
6a5a0e58029d56b0ffa195ab60b3d01403125b50.body:
Fix \(r\in\mathbb N\) and real constants
\(\delta,C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\) with \(\psi_{\xi}>0\). There exist constants
\(c_0,C_0,\tau,c_{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_0,\qquad 0<C_0,\qquad 0<\tau\le \psi_{\xi},\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]
For every parameter record \(p\) whose displayed fields satisfy
\[
p.r=r,\quad p.\delta=\delta,\quad p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\quad
p.C_g=C_g,\quad p.C_q=C_q,\quad
p.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\quad p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},
\]
and every \(n\ge 1\), if the non-Gaussian class in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\) is nonempty, then there are a base law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed observed treatment law.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) equals its law under \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed regressions and supplied codes.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\) and the clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) equal those under \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome equation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely under \(P_{n,\vartheta}\).
\item \textbf{(Product relative entropy.)} For all real \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and
\[
|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=\frac{h}{\sqrt n},
\]
one has
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Moreover, for every starting law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) in the class of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\), there is a family \(\{P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}:|\vartheta|\le c_0\}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(JMS ACE membership and target.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and \(\theta_0(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}})=\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed observed treatment law.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the law of \((X,T)\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) equals its law under \(P^{\circ}\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed nuisance objects.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the functions \(g_0,q_0\), the clipped supplied codes \(\bar g_n,\bar q_n\), and the treatment innovation \(\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) equal those under \(P^{\circ}\), and the treatment and outcome code-radius conditions in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class}\) hold at \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
\item \textbf{(Gaussian outcome innovation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\), the outcome innovation \(\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0\eta\) under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) has law \(N(0,\tau^2)\) and is independent of \((X,T)\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome equation.)} For every \(|\vartheta|\le c_0\),
\[
Y=q_0(X)+\vartheta\,\eta+\xi
\]
almost surely under \(P_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\).
\item \textbf{(Product relative entropy.)} For all real \(\vartheta_0,\vartheta_1,h\) with \(|\vartheta_0|\le c_0\), \(|\vartheta_1|\le c_0\), and
\[
|\vartheta_1-\vartheta_0|=\frac{h}{\sqrt n},
\]
one has
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{n,\vartheta_0}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\,\middle\|\,(P_{n,\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{ACE}})^{\otimes n}\right)
\le C_0 h^2 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Finally, for every pair of clipped-code functions \(g_{\star},q_{\star}:Xspace\to\mathbb R\), if there is a law \(P^{\circ}\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) with \(\bar g_n=g_{\star}\) and \(\bar q_n=q_{\star}\), then the fixed-code JMS ACE minimax risk satisfies
\[
\frac{c_{\mathrm{ACE}}}{n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n;\bar g_n,\bar q_n)}
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}:\\ \bar g_n=g_{\star},\ \bar q_n=q_{\star}}}
E_P\!\left[\{\widetilde\theta-\theta_0(P)\}^2\right].
\]

c8a8f8431648d74337325846af63b8463b0a6d72.title: ACE class relations
c8a8f8431648d74337325846af63b8463b0a6d72.body:
Fix a parameter tuple \(p\) with positive sample-size component, ACE order \(r\), cumulant order \(k=r+1\) with \(2\le r\), comparison exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) with \(r\le s\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \((\varepsilon_{1,n})_{n\ge1}\) and \((\varepsilon_{2,n})_{n\ge1}\). For every class index \(n\) and every model instance \(m\) satisfying the usual measurability and integrability conditions,
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
\]
where the classes are those of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class}. Also,
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}},
\]
where \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) is the subclass in \cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}. If \(s=r\), then for every such model instance \(m\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]

0e1bd12a051da8925f9135288a7760a6d99755ff.title: Bounded Gaussian degeneracy

73f48b196927f7a2a1437dd10810f3bc7f8c1cd3.title: Clipped ratio risk decomposition
73f48b196927f7a2a1437dd10810f3bc7f8c1cd3.body:
Using the empirical-average notation \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f(O_i)\) from \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, let the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample.)} \(n\ge 1\), and \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) is an arbitrary sample in an observation space \(\Omega\).
\item \textbf{(Scores.)} \(W,R:\Omega\to\mathbb R\) are real-valued functions.
\item \textbf{(Constants.)} \(\theta,C_{\theta},A,\mu_W\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|\theta|\le C_{\theta}\), \(A>0\), and \(A/2\le \mu_W\).
\item \textbf{(Clipped ratio.)} \(\widehat\theta\) is the statistic
\[
\widehat\theta
=
\begin{cases}
\min\!\left\{\max\!\left\{(\theta\,\mathbb P_n W+\mathbb P_n R)/\mathbb P_n W,\,-C_{\theta}\right\},\,C_{\theta}\right\},
& A/4\le \mathbb P_n W,\\
0, & \mathbb P_n W<A/4.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
(\widehat\theta-\theta)^2
\le
\frac{16}{A^2}
\left\{
(\mathbb P_n R)^2
+
C_{\theta}^2(\mathbb P_n(W-\mu_W))^2
\right\}.
\]

3d8a4e04c83e881c4c543b66a752317af4c79ba7.title: Population numerator envelope
3d8a4e04c83e881c4c543b66a752317af4c79ba7.body:
Let \(p\) be a parameter record as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, with sample size \(n\), primitive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and outer search radius \(R_1\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}. Define
\[
C_G(p)=\left[64\{C_q^4+4C_{\theta}^4\psi_{\eta}^4+4\psi_{\xi}^4\}+2\exp\{16R_1C_g+16R_1^2\psi_{\eta}^2\}\right]^{1/2}.
\]
Let \(m\) be a model with observed-data law \(P\) as in \cref{obj:def:plm-model}. Suppose that \(P\) belongs to the non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}, where \(n\) is the sample size in \(p\). Then, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\) with \(|z|\le R_1\), the observable outcome-weighted transform \(G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}]\) from \cref{obj:def:contour-functional} satisfies
\[
|G_n(z)|\le C_G(p).
\]

3351c6ae95c3c20de58ebab0eed88454e12edd5a.title: Luxemburg MGF envelope
3351c6ae95c3c20de58ebab0eed88454e12edd5a.body:
Use the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian norm convention of \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}. Let \(\psi>0\) be a Luxemburg scale, and let \(W\) be a real-valued random variable on a probability space with law \(P\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regularity.)} \(W\) is measurable, \(W\in L^1(P)\), and \(\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\in L^1(P)\).
\item \textbf{(Luxemburg envelope.)} \(E_P\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\le 2\).
\item \textbf{(Centering.)} \(E_P W=0\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P e^{tW}\le \exp(4\psi^2t^2).
\]

853b64924065b6294abf0cc02bf0714e7b5ff2c8.title: Gaussian degeneracy
853b64924065b6294abf0cc02bf0714e7b5ff2c8.body:
Fix a parameter tuple with positive sample size \(n\), integers \(r\) and \(k\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge 2\), an exponent \(s\ge r\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices, with values \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) at the sample size. On any measurable covariate space, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degenerate target.)} For every model \(m\) whose law \(P\) lies in the bounded-outcome Gaussian JMS comparison class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) of \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}, the partially linear coefficient obeys
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero fixed-code risks.)} For any supplied deterministic code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\), suppose the fixed-code Gaussian JMS class contains at least one model \(m\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) for which the clipped supplied treatment and outcome codes agree pointwise at index \(n\):
\[
\bar g_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
\bar q_n(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}
\]
for every covariate value \(x\). Then
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

bfca820486f33c3cbe1dad817645accc0fe3fe9d.title: Luxemburg MGF envelope
bfca820486f33c3cbe1dad817645accc0fe3fe9d.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law and let \(\psi>0\). Let \(W\) be a real-valued random variable under \(P\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regularity.)} \(W\) is measurable and \(W\in L^1(P)\).
\item \textbf{(Centering.)} \(E_P W=0\).
\item \textbf{(Luxemburg envelope.)} Under the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian convention of \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, \(\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\in L^1(P)\) and
\[
E_P\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\le 2.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P e^{tW}\le \exp(4\psi^2t^2).
\]

7730666e3b77a7c1a7d31d5a7fdcec4d73bb6b1b.title: Clipped ratio risk decomposition
7730666e3b77a7c1a7d31d5a7fdcec4d73bb6b1b.body:
Let \(\Omega\) be any observation space. For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\in\Omega\), write the empirical average as \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f(O_i)\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-parameters}\). Let \(W,R:\Omega\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\theta\), \(C_{\theta}\), \(A\), and \(\mu_W\) be real numbers. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Clipping range.)} The target value \(\theta\) lies inside the clipping radius \(C_{\theta}\): \(|\theta|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Denominator scale.)} \(A>0\).
\item \textbf{(Population denominator mean.)} \(\mu_W\ge A/2\).
\end{itemize}
Define the clipped ratio statistic at threshold \(A/4\) by
\[
\widehat\theta
=
\begin{cases}
\min\!\left\{\max\!\left\{\dfrac{\theta\,\mathbb P_n W+\mathbb P_n R}{\mathbb P_n W},-C_{\theta}\right\},C_{\theta}\right\},
& A/4\le \mathbb P_n W,\\[1.1em]
0,
& A/4>\mathbb P_n W.
\end{cases}
\]
Then, for every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\in\Omega\),
\[
(\widehat\theta-\theta)^2
\le
\frac{16}{A^2}
\left\{
(\mathbb P_n R)^2
+
C_{\theta}^2\bigl(\mathbb P_n(W-\mu_W)\bigr)^2
\right\}.
\]

4ff3a52baca6d8bcf231dedff3e886ab5b7ca6da.title: ACE class relations
4ff3a52baca6d8bcf231dedff3e886ab5b7ca6da.body:
Fix a parameter tuple \(p\) with ACE order \(r\), cumulant order \(k=r+1\), \(2\le r\), comparison exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) satisfying \(r\le s\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices. Fix any class index \(n\in\mathbb N\). For every model record \(m\), with observed-data law \(P=m.P\), regression functions \(g_0,q_0\), and supplied deterministic code sequences \(\widehat g,\widehat q\) satisfying the usual measurability, probability, conditional-mean, and integrability conditions, the class predicates of \cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class,obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass} satisfy
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}.
\]
They also satisfy
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
If \(s=r\), then for every such model record \(m\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]

0a0be1c19918c087138ffa61c5fbb515ccb0a75a.title: Gaussian JMS degeneracy
0a0be1c19918c087138ffa61c5fbb515ccb0a75a.body:
Fix a measurable covariate space and a parameter tuple with \(n\ge 1\), integers \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge 2\), an exponent \(s\ge r\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) that are nonnegative and nonincreasing on positive indices, with values \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\) and \(\varepsilon_{2,n}\) at sample size \(n\). Then the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degenerate target.)} Every model \(P\) in the bounded-outcome Gaussian JMS class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) has
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero fixed-code risks.)} For any deterministic supplied code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\), suppose the fixed-code restriction of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) contains a model whose clipped treatment and outcome codes at index \(n\) agree pointwise with
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

b4d8fcc2af2a913dce2c8c0cdbd74dc8775805b9.title: ACE class inclusions
b4d8fcc2af2a913dce2c8c0cdbd74dc8775805b9.body:
Fix the following objects and conventions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameters.)} Let \(p\) be a parameter tuple with ACE order \(r\), cumulant order \(k=r+1\), \(2\le r\), comparison exponent \(s\in[0,\infty]\) with \(r\le s\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices.
\item \textbf{(Class index.)} Let \(n\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Models.)} Consider model records \(m\) on the measurable covariate space, with observed-data law \(P=m.P\), regression functions \(g_0,q_0\), supplied deterministic code sequences \(\widehat g,\widehat q\), and the usual measurability, probability, conditional-mean, and integrability conditions.
\item \textbf{(Classes.)} Interpret \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\) as the class predicates in \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class,obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every such model record \(m\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}.
\]
Also, for every such model record \(m\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
If \(s=r\), then, for every such model record \(m\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}} .
\]

872d19729d996e72cd98316c931d1a25e1c04aee.title: Gaussian degeneracy
872d19729d996e72cd98316c931d1a25e1c04aee.body:
Fix any parameter tuple with sample size \(n\ge 1\), integers \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge 2\), an exponent \(s\ge r\), a probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) that are nonnegative and nonincreasing on positive indices. On any measurable covariate space, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degenerate target.)} For every model \(m\) with law \(P\) in the bounded-outcome Gaussian JMS comparison class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class},
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero fixed-code risks.)} For any supplied code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\), suppose there is at least one model \(m\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} whose clipped treatment and outcome codes agree pointwise at index \(n\) with the clipped supplied codes
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Then the displayed-parameter Gaussian JMS minimax mean-squared risk and generalized-quantile risk both vanish:
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

869902968208ecb827000fc6c82c148b8e6458ee.title: Selected contour perturbation bound
869902968208ecb827000fc6c82c148b8e6458ee.body:
Fix \(p\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, the primitive certified record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}, the range certified record \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, a treatment-regression code sequence, and observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with \(O=(X,T,Y)\) as in \cref{obj:def:plm-model}. Let \(B\) be the contour bank generated from \(p\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), with radii \(\rho_j\) and lower-modulus certificate \(a_{\star}\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) be the canonical certified statistic of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}. Let \(F,G:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\), let \(d,e,C_G,\mu,\nu\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|\vartheta|\le C_{\theta}\).

Assume the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Selector event.)} The canonical selector event holds: \(d\ge0\), \(e\ge0\), \(C_G\ge0\), \(\mu>0\), \(\nu>0\),
\[
\mu=\frac{31a_{\star}}{64},
\qquad
\nu=\frac{23a_{\star}}{64},
\qquad
d\le \mu-\nu,
\]
and, for the canonical represented input built from the sample, there are a bank index \(j\) and an integer \(N\ge1\) such that the selector chooses \(C_j\), the pilot pass at \(C_j\) decodes to \(N\), the evaluation-fold modulus lower endpoint at \(C_j\) is at least \(a_{\star}/4\), and every \(z\in C_j\) satisfies
\[
\mu\le |F(z)|,\qquad |G(z)|\le C_G,\qquad
|\widehat F_{1,n}(z)-F(z)|\le d,\qquad
|\widehat G_{1,n}(z)-G(z)|\le e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Selected-circle integrability.)} For every bank index \(j\) selected by the canonical program, the functions
\[
z\mapsto \frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z\mapsto \frac{G(z)}{F(z)}
\]
are contour integrable on \(C_j\).
\item \textbf{(Selected-circle identification.)} For every bank index \(j\) selected by the canonical program and every decoded pilot integer \(N\), the target is identified by
\[
\vartheta
=
\Re\left[
\{N\,2\pi i\}^{-1}
\oint_{C_j}\frac{G(z)}{F(z)}\,dz
\right].
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\vartheta\right|
\le
R_1\max\{\nu^{-1},\,C_G(\mu\nu)^{-1}\}(d+e)
+\frac{1}{\max\{n,1\}} .
\]

fe317068d1226cf2ac9edc1af65d2d7544011f52.title: Gaussian class degeneracy
fe317068d1226cf2ac9edc1af65d2d7544011f52.body:
Fix a parameter tuple with:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} A positive sample size \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Orders and exponent.)} Integers \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge 2\), and an exponent \(s\ge r\).
\item \textbf{(Probability level.)} A level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} Constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma>0\).
\item \textbf{(Code-radius sequences.)} Sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) whose values are nonnegative on positive indices and nonincreasing on positive indices.
\end{itemize}
On any measurable covariate space, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degenerate target.)} Every model \(m\) in the bounded-outcome Gaussian JMS comparison class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} has
\[
\theta_0(P)=0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero minimax risks.)} For any supplied deterministic code sequences \(\widehat g=(\widehat g_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\) and \(\widehat q=(\widehat q_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}\), suppose there is a model \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:gaussian-class} whose clipped supplied treatment and outcome codes agree pointwise at index \(n\) with
\[
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
x\mapsto \min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)=0.
\]
\end{itemize}

36781849ec02e340f17dae6880d32c9a489d5c60.title: Luxemburg MGF envelope
36781849ec02e340f17dae6880d32c9a489d5c60.body:
Use the Luxemburg sub-Gaussian convention of \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}. Let \(W\) be a real-valued random variable on a probability space with law \(P\), and let \(\psi>0\) be a scale parameter. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regularity.)} \(W\) is measurable and \(W\in L^1(P)\).
\item \textbf{(Centeredness.)} \(E_P W=0\).
\item \textbf{(Luxemburg exponential square envelope.)} The random variable \(\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\) is \(P\)-integrable and satisfies
\[
E_P\exp(W^2/\psi^2)\le 2.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P e^{tW}\le \exp(4\psi^2t^2).
\]

7d53e8402cfc555664ec983018f71f03a3cd52de.title: Observable transform factorization
7d53e8402cfc555664ec983018f71f03a3cd52de.body:
Let \(m\) be a model instance with observed-data law \(P\) in the non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). Define, for \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=E_P[e^{zZ_n}],\qquad
M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}],\qquad
H_n(z)=E_P[e^{zD_n(X)}],
\]
where \(Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X)\), \(\eta=T-g_0(X)\), and \(D_n(X)=g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X)\). With \(b_n(X)=q_0(X)-\theta_0D_n(X)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:outcome-contamination}\), also define
\[
G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}],\qquad
B_n(z)=E_P[b_n(X)e^{zD_n(X)}].
\]
Then, for every \(z\in\mathbb C\),
\[
F_n(z)=M(z)H_n(z)
\]
and
\[
G_n(z)=\theta_0 F_n'(z)+M(z)B_n(z).
\]

58750fa2026811fdbd5fe46fd2a9df86157a7624.title: Zero instrument identities
58750fa2026811fdbd5fe46fd2a9df86157a7624.body:
Fix parameters \(p\), a model \(m\) with observed-data law \(P\), and a sample size \(n\).  Let
\[
M(z)=E_P[\exp\{z\eta\}],\qquad
Z_n=T-\bar g_n(X),\qquad
H_n(z)=E_P[\exp\{z(g_0(X)-\bar g_n(X))\}].
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class membership.)} \(n\ge 1\) and \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Zero multiplicity.)} \(\ell\ge 1\), \(z_0\in\mathbb C\), \(M(z_0)=0\), and the analytic order of \(M\) at \(z_0\) is \(\ell\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument.)} \(J_{z_0,\ell}\) is the zero-based instrument of \(\cref{obj:def:zero-instrument}\),
\[
J_{z_0,\ell}(w)=w^{\ell-1}\exp(z_0w).
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the following identities hold:
\[
\forall d\in\mathbb R,\qquad
E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(\eta+d)\right]=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
E_P\!\left[J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\mid X\right]=0
\quad P\text{-almost surely},
\]
and
\[
E_P\!\left[Z_n J_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]
=
M^{(\ell)}(z_0)H_n(z_0).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(E_P[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)]\neq0\),
\[
\theta_0
=
\frac{E_P\!\left[YJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]}
{E_P\!\left[Z_nJ_{z_0,\ell}(Z_n)\right]}.
\]

41f1c91fc02317a1b6d3e116d9bb377f0e6e2ebf.title: Population numerator envelope
41f1c91fc02317a1b6d3e116d9bb377f0e6e2ebf.body:
Let \(p\) be a parameter record with sample size \(n\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, and let \(R_1\) denote the outer search radius attached to \(p\) in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}. Define
\[
C_G(p)
=
\left[
64\{C_q^4+4C_{\theta}^4\psi_{\eta}^4+4\psi_{\xi}^4\}
+
2\exp\{16R_1C_g+16R_1^2\psi_{\eta}^2\}
\right]^{1/2}.
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(m\) is a model with observed-data law \(P\), parameter \(\theta_0\), regressions \(g_0,q_0\), and deterministic code sequences \(\widehat g,\widehat q\), as in \cref{obj:def:plm-model}.
\item \textbf{(Class membership.)} The model \(m\) belongs to the non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) at the parameter record \(p\), in the sense of \cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}.
\item \textbf{(Search window.)} The complex argument \(z\in\mathbb C\) satisfies \(|z|\le R_1\).
\end{itemize}
For the observable outcome-weighted transform
\[
G_n(z)=E_P[Ye^{zZ_n}]
\]
from \cref{obj:def:contour-functional}, one has
\[
|G_n(z)|\le C_G(p).
\]

a65d3c24e2602345cc7170ca008c4fbf18a91103.title: Finite contour bank
a65d3c24e2602345cc7170ca008c4fbf18a91103.body:
Fix a parameter record \(p\) with primitive constants and code-radius sequences as in \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}\), and fix a certified-real contour-bank handle \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) for \(p\).  Let \(n\ge 1\), let \(m\) be a model on a general measurable covariate space, and suppose that \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).  Let \(B\) be the bank data assembled from \(p\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) by \(\cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}\).  Then \(a_{\star}>0\), the bank constants satisfy
\[
N_{\mathrm{cert}}=4U_{\psi}^{2}(U_R+2)^3,\qquad
m_{\star}=N_{\mathrm{cert}}+3,\qquad
J=2^{m_{\star}-1}+1,
\]
\[
d_{\star}=2^{-m_{\star}},\qquad
h_{\star}=d_{\star}/3,\qquad
e_{\star}=8U_RU_{\psi}^{2}(U_R+1)^2,
\]
and
\[
d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}=3(2U_R+1),\qquad
u_{\star}=2e_{\star}+N_{\mathrm{cert}}\{m_{\star}+d_{\star}^{\mathrm{den}}\},\qquad
a_{\star,\mathbb Q}=2^{-u_{\star}}.
\]
The certified radii \(\rho_j\), \(j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\), are strictly increasing and obey
\[
R_0<\rho_j<R_1
\]
for every \(j\).  Moreover, for the treatment-innovation moment-generating function \(M(z)=E_P[e^{z\eta}]\), there is an index \(j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\) such that the circle \(C_j=\{z:|z|=\rho_j\}\) has
\[
N_{C_j}(M)>0
\]
and
\[
a_{\star}\le |M(z)|\qquad\text{for every }z\in C_j .
\]

c7d36fd43d58022fd5c52a050e8c90a0e7178d49.title: Clipped ratio risk decomposition
c7d36fd43d58022fd5c52a050e8c90a0e7178d49.body:
Let \(W\) and \(R\) be real-valued functions on the observation space, let \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) be any sample, and write \(\mathbb P_n f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f(O_i)\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Target and clipping bound.)} The target value \(\theta\) and clipping bound \(C_{\theta}\) satisfy \(|\theta|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Denominator level.)} The scale \(A\) satisfies \(A>0\).
\item \textbf{(Population denominator mean.)} The denominator mean \(\mu_W\) satisfies \(\mu_W\ge A/2\).
\end{itemize}
Define the clipped ratio statistic at threshold \(A/4\) by
\[
\widehat\theta
=
\begin{cases}
\min\!\left\{\max\!\left\{\dfrac{\theta\,\mathbb P_n W+\mathbb P_n R}{\mathbb P_n W},-C_{\theta}\right\},C_{\theta}\right\},
& A/4\le \mathbb P_n W,\\[1.2ex]
0,
& \mathbb P_n W<A/4 .
\end{cases}
\]
Then
\[
(\widehat\theta-\theta)^2
\le
\frac{16}{A^2}
\left\{
(\mathbb P_n R)^2
+
C_{\theta}^2(\mathbb P_n W-\mu_W)^2
\right\}.
\]

4bdd20c61866d7d472a972e467ecd8ed0c9f19ef.title: Selected contour perturbation
4bdd20c61866d7d472a972e467ecd8ed0c9f19ef.body:
Fix a parameter record \(p\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-parameters}, the primitive certified record \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}, the range record \(\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, a supplied treatment-regression code sequence, and observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with \(O=(X,T,Y)\) as in \cref{obj:def:plm-model}. Let \(B\) be the contour bank generated by \(p\) and \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\), with radii \(\rho_j\), dyadic lower-modulus certificate \(a_{\star}\), and outer radius \(R_1\) as in \cref{obj:def:contour-bank-handle}. Let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) be the certified adaptive contour statistic of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, evaluated on the canonicalized sample, and let \(\widehat F_{1,n}\) and \(\widehat G_{1,n}\) be the evaluation-fold empirical transforms of \cref{obj:def:local-gaussian-handle}. Let \(F,G:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\), let \(d,e,C_G,\mu,\nu\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|\vartheta|\le C_{\theta}\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Good event.)} \(d\ge0\), \(e\ge0\), \(C_G\ge0\), \(\mu>0\), \(\nu>0\),
\[
\mu=\frac{31a_{\star}}{64},
\qquad
\nu=\frac{23a_{\star}}{64},
\qquad
d\le\mu-\nu .
\]
Moreover, for the canonical represented input \(\mathfrak s_{\star}\) of \cref{obj:def:adaptive-contour-estimator}, there are a bank index \(j\) and an integer \(N_j\ge1\) such that the selector chooses \(C_j\), the pilot winding rectangle at \(C_j\) decodes to \(N_j\), the evaluation-fold lower-modulus enclosure at \(C_j\) has lower endpoint at least \(a_{\star}/4\), and every \(z\in C_j\) satisfies
\[
\mu\le |F(z)|,\qquad
|G(z)|\le C_G,\qquad
|\widehat F_{1,n}(z)-F(z)|\le d,\qquad
|\widehat G_{1,n}(z)-G(z)|\le e .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contour integrability.)} For every bank index \(j\), if the selector chooses \(C_j\), then \(\widehat G_{1,n}/\widehat F_{1,n}\) and \(G/F\) are contour integrable on \(C_j\).
\item \textbf{(Exact identification.)} For every bank index \(j\) and integer \(N\), if the selector chooses \(C_j\) and the pilot winding rectangle at \(C_j\) decodes to \(N\), then
\[
\vartheta
=
\Re\left[
\{N\,2\pi i\}^{-1}
\oint_{C_j}\frac{G(z)}{F(z)}\,dz
\right].
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}-\vartheta\right|
\le
R_1\max\{\nu^{-1},\,C_G(\mu\nu)^{-1}\}(d+e)
+\frac{1}{\max\{n,1\}} .
\]

2a27ac2c66fb270c4ccfd9053e34c215b229a237.title: Uniform transform concentration
2a27ac2c66fb270c4ccfd9053e34c215b229a237.body:
For any measurable covariate space and any real constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi}\), and \(R_1\), there is a constant \(K>0\), depending only on these displayed constants, such that the following holds.  Let \(p\) be a parameter record satisfying
\[
p.C_{\theta}=C_{\theta},\qquad
p.C_g=C_g,\qquad
p.C_q=C_q,\qquad
p.\psi_{\eta}=\psi_{\eta},\qquad
p.\psi_{\xi}=\psi_{\xi},
\]
with search radius \(R_1\), and with sample size \(n=p.n\ge2\).  Let \(m\) be a model whose law \(P\) belongs to the non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\), and suppose the sample law is the i.i.d. product law \(P^{\otimes n}\) as in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).  Then, for each fold \(a\in\{0,1\}\) with \(I_a\ne\varnothing\),
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\left\{\sup_{\lvert z\rvert\le R_1}
\left|\widehat F_{a,n}(z)-F_n(z)\right|\right\}^{2}
\right]
+
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\left\{\sup_{\lvert z\rvert\le R_1}
\left|\widehat G_{a,n}(z)-G_n(z)\right|\right\}^{2}
\right]
\le
\frac{K}{\lvert I_a\rvert}.
\]

624771b53033b8ab71c01a1352ecdb26daa4b408.title: Gaussian degeneracy under bounds
624771b53033b8ab71c01a1352ecdb26daa4b408.body:
Fix a general measurable covariate space and a parameter tuple \(p\) with sample size \(n\ge1\), orders \(r,k\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(k=r+1\) and \(r\ge2\), exponent \(s\ge r\), probability level \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices.

For every model instance \(m\), membership in the bounded-outcome Gaussian JMS class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) specified by \(\cref{obj:def:gaussian-class}\) implies
\[
\theta_0(m)=0.
\]
Moreover, for any deterministic supplied code sequences \(\widehat g,\widehat q:\mathbb N\to\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), suppose that the fixed-code Gaussian JMS class contains at least one model \(m\) such that \(m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm G,n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}\) and, for every \(x\),
\[
\bar g_n^{m}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat g_n(x),-C_g\},C_g\},
\qquad
\bar q_n^{m}(x)=\min\{\max\{\widehat q_n(x),-C_q\},C_q\}.
\]
Then the displayed-parameter Gaussian JMS minimax MSE and generalized-quantile risks for these clipped codes both vanish:
\[
\mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
\mathfrak M_{n,1-\gamma}^{\mathrm G}(p;\widehat g,\widehat q)
=
0.
\]

c315598d2bf4f4b185b74c32716a67f22b7864d6.title: ACE class relations
c315598d2bf4f4b185b74c32716a67f22b7864d6.body:
Fix primitive parameters \(p\) with \(r,k\in\mathbb N\), \(k=r+1\), \(r\ge2\), \(s\in[0,\infty]\) satisfying \(s\ge r\), \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), positive constants
\[
C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma>0,
\]
and nonnegative nonincreasing code-radius sequences \(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices.  Then, for every class index \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every model \(m\) on the measurable covariate space,
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n},
\]
where the two classes are those of \(\cref{obj:def:jms-ace-class,obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\).  Moreover, for the \(L^s(P_X)\)-restricted ACE comparison subclass of \(\cref{obj:def:ace-comparison-subclass}\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}.
\]
If \(s=r\), then for every such \(m\),
\[
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ACE},n}^{\mathrm{JMS}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}.
\]

cbf9120219a752449afafae25ec679a15064b4e3.title: I.i.d. sampling
cbf9120219a752449afafae25ec679a15064b4e3.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the observations satisfy
\[
O_1,\ldots,O_n \stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim} P .
\]

47e46056cf0c46973c86e39b51ebbc238c747415.title: Independent treatment noise
47e46056cf0c46973c86e39b51ebbc238c747415.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the treatment innovation is independent of the covariates:
\[
\eta \perp X .
\]

7f4fc8e17a5bea0a071726017d88a0eb9eabf67d.title: Outcome mean independence
7f4fc8e17a5bea0a071726017d88a0eb9eabf67d.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the outcome innovation satisfies
\[
E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0
\]
almost surely.

45815dc206f335f7ef9e2d05afc3e212210774fc.title: Coefficient range
45815dc206f335f7ef9e2d05afc3e212210774fc.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the partially linear coefficient satisfies
\[
|\theta_0|\le C_{\theta}.
\]

bfc942e601c12d4a72bd987f13680b1787d84a15.title: Treatment regression range
bfc942e601c12d4a72bd987f13680b1787d84a15.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the treatment regression satisfies
\[
\|g_0\|_{\infty}\le C_g.
\]

955e1c25949740dc0868b3213c6635fe384fa00f.title: Outcome regression range
955e1c25949740dc0868b3213c6635fe384fa00f.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the outcome regression satisfies
\[
\|q_0\|_{\infty}\le C_q.
\]

b53cf2239e486ab343a009ec78f4bc7c2913c8f7.title: Bounded Gaussian outcome
b53cf2239e486ab343a009ec78f4bc7c2913c8f7.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the outcome coordinate is bounded by
\[
|Y|\le C_q
\]
\(P\)-almost surely.

761b88c507adbe4458e9b37e7e642862823ee6a5.title: Treatment innovation sub-Gaussianity
761b88c507adbe4458e9b37e7e642862823ee6a5.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, with the Luxemburg convention
\[
\lVert W\rVert_{\psi_2}
=
\inf\{u>0:E_P[\exp(W^2/u^2)]\le 2\},
\]
the treatment innovation \(\eta\) satisfies
\[
\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}.
\]

bb4c664724a617c9f447d598dfa27d29f65aeabb.title: Outcome innovation conditional sub-Gaussianity
bb4c664724a617c9f447d598dfa27d29f65aeabb.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the outcome innovation \(\xi\) satisfies
\[
\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}
\]
\(P\)-almost surely.

3a6c433d871082882a7b2d54dcf590cdb27918ac.title: Treatment cumulant separation
3a6c433d871082882a7b2d54dcf590cdb27918ac.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, the \(k\)th cumulant of the treatment innovation satisfies
\[
|\kappa_k(\eta)|\ge\delta.
\]

9d84e4326828fe7dc638879ef539135026b9654d.title: Treatment-code radius
9d84e4326828fe7dc638879ef539135026b9654d.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\),
\[
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}.
\]

639fe11549abeb7c90642d50c631162e960a1f4e.title: Outcome-code radius
639fe11549abeb7c90642d50c631162e960a1f4e.body:
For the model and parameters in \cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\),
\[
\lVert \bar q_n-q_0\rVert_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}.
\]

7e4f086f794cc71d08281f37a428a4a0a683143a.title: Gaussian treatment innovation
7e4f086f794cc71d08281f37a428a4a0a683143a.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the treatment innovation satisfies
\[
\eta\sim N(0,\sigma^2).
\]

4af10386ca83a41e473c98410815765b7ad2448a.title: Non-Gaussian class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\)
4af10386ca83a41e473c98410815765b7ad2448a.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:independent-treatment-noise,obj:ass:outcome-mean-independence,obj:ass:theta-range,obj:ass:g-range,obj:ass:q-range,obj:ass:eta-subgaussian,obj:ass:xi-subgaussian,obj:ass:cumulant-separation,obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), the class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) consists of observed-data laws \(P\) for which, with
\[
g_0(x)=E_P[T\mid X=x],\qquad
q_0(x)=E_P[Y\mid X=x],
\]
\[
E_P[Y\mid X,T]=q_0(X)+\theta_0(P)\{T-g_0(X)\},
\]
and
\[
\eta=T-g_0(X),\qquad
\xi=Y-q_0(X)-\theta_0(P)\eta,
\]
the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Independence.)} \(\eta\perp X\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome mean.)} \(E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient range.)} \(|\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta}\).
\item \textbf{(Regression ranges.)} \(\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g\) and \(\lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q\).
\item \textbf{(Innovation tails.)} \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta}\) and \(\lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi}\).
\item \textbf{(Cumulant separation.)} \(|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-code radius.)} \(\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}
=
\left\{
P:
\begin{array}{l}
\eta\perp X,\quad E_P[\xi\mid X,T]=0,\quad |\theta_0(P)|\le C_{\theta},\\
\lVert g_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_g,\quad \lVert q_0\rVert_{\infty}\le C_q,\\
\lVert\eta\rVert_{\psi_2}\le\psi_{\eta},\quad \lVert\xi\rVert_{\psi_2\mid X}\le\psi_{\xi},\\
|\kappa_{r+1}(\eta)|\ge\delta,\quad
\lVert \bar g_n-g_0\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n}
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]

fe872429d034d25b121b23980dfa9c60c7ee13d0.title: Generalized quantile \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\)
fe872429d034d25b121b23980dfa9c60c7ee13d0.body:
Under \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:def:plm-model,obj:def:model-parameters}\), for an observed-data law \(P\), a sample size \(n\ge 1\), and a real-valued statistic \(W=W(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), the generalized lower \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile is
\[
Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)
=
\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:F_W(t)\ge 1-\gamma\}.
\]
Here \(F_W(t)=\Pr(W\le t)\) denotes the distribution function of \(W\) under the i.i.d. product law \(P^{\otimes n}\), and \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\). Thus \(Q_{P,1-\gamma}(W)\) is the left-continuous generalized inverse of \(F_W\) evaluated at level \(1-\gamma\).

20e666dc4c2419cb035a1fb37ac2e7d6e292ee69.title: JMS eligibility condition \(\mathsf E_n^{\mathrm{JMS}}\)

71710a958c7135b3f551146969069fded8a3e22d.title: ACE comparison subclass \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}\)
71710a958c7135b3f551146969069fded8a3e22d.body:
Define
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}^{\mathrm{ACE}}
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}:
\|\bar g_n-g_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{1,n},
\ 
\|\bar q_n-q_0\|_{L^s(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{2,n}
\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NG},n}\) is the spectral class in \(\cref{obj:def:non-gaussian-class}\). This class retains the spectral restrictions and imposes the two supplied-code bounds displayed above.

ebff8c6072ac59c1fcb78d22828c5b434863ccf8.title: Certified contour arithmetic substrate \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\)
ebff8c6072ac59c1fcb78d22828c5b434863ccf8.body:
The bounded-build specification \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) consists of the following finite arithmetic operations and their soundness contracts.

A represented real number is given by rational closed intervals \(I_m=[I_m^-,I_m^+]\), an executable modulus \(\mu:\mathbb Q_{>0}\to\mathbb N\), and the semantic conditions
\[
x\in I_{m+1}\subseteq I_m,
\qquad
I_{\mu(e)}^+-I_{\mu(e)}^-\le e .
\]
A positive represented real additionally supplies a rational \(p>0\) such that \(p\le x\). Executable routines use the interval, modulus, and positivity data.

For rational intervals \(A=[a_-,a_+]\) and \(B=[b_-,b_+]\), define
\[
A+B=[a_-+b_-,a_++b_+],
\qquad
A-B=[a_--b_+,a_+-b_-],
\]
and
\[
AB=
\left[
\min\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\},
\max\{a_-b_-,a_-b_+,a_+b_-,a_+b_+\}
\right].
\]
A complex rectangle is \(A+iB\). Complex addition, subtraction, conjugation, and multiplication are obtained from these endpoint operations, with
\[
(A+iB)(C+iD)=(AC-BD)+i(AD+BC).
\]
For \(A=[a_-,a_+]\), set
\[
\operatorname{sq}_{-}(A)=
\begin{cases}
0,&a_-\le0\le a_+,\\
\min\{a_-^2,a_+^2\},&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
\operatorname{sq}_{+}(A)=\max\{a_-^2,a_+^2\}.
\]
Thus \(|A+iB|^2\) is enclosed by adding the corresponding lower and upper square bounds. Rational bisection between nonnegative rational endpoints gives lower and upper square-root enclosures whose width after \(q\) bisections is at most the initial width times \(2^{-q}\). Division is the guarded operation
\[
\frac{A+iB}{C+iD}
=(A+iB)(C-iD)(C^2+D^2)^{-1},
\]
performed when the modulus routine returns a rational lower bound \(m>0\), followed by outward division by the positive rational interval enclosing \(C^2+D^2\).

The represented value of \(\pi\) is constructed from Machin's identity
\[
\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239).
\]
For \(0<x<1\),
\[
\arctan x
=
\sum_{j=0}^{N}(-1)^j\frac{x^{2j+1}}{2j+1}
+
R_N(x),
\qquad
|R_N(x)|\le\frac{x^{2N+3}}{2N+3}.
\]
Intersecting the first \(m+1\) requested rational enclosures gives nested intervals. If \(e=p/q>0\) is in lowest terms, the choice \(N=5q+5\) makes the propagated Machin remainder smaller than \(e\).

For a rational interval contained in \([-B,B]\), with rational \(B\ge0\), evaluate the Taylor polynomials for \(\exp\), \(\sin\), and \(\cos\) by the preceding interval operations, with Lagrange remainders bounded by
\[
3^{\lceil B\rceil}\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
\qquad
\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},
\qquad
\frac{B^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.
\]
For a requested rational error \(e=p/q>0\), take
\[
N=\lceil2B\rceil+q+2\lceil B\rceil+2.
\]
After the index \(\lceil2B\rceil\), successive absolute Taylor terms decrease by at least a factor \(1/2\); since \(3^{\lceil B\rceil}<2^{2\lceil B\rceil}\) and \(2^{-q}\le q^{-1}\le e\), this \(N\) gives error at most \(e\). Finite intersections make the output rectangles nested. Therefore
\[
\exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)\{\cos y+i\sin y\}
\]
has a nested complex-rectangle extension with an effective modulus on every bounded input rectangle. Combining the constructed representation of \(\pi\) with these trigonometric operations gives, from a positive radius representation \(\mathfrak r\) and integers \(N\ge1\), \(0\le q<N\), represented circle nodes for
\[
r\exp(2\pi iq/N)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
2\pi i r\exp(2\pi iq/N).
\]

Finite rectangle sums and products are primitive recursive. If a complex-valued function on \([0,1]\) has a supplied rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), then the uniform mesh
\[
N_{\mathrm{mesh}}=\lceil L/e\rceil+1
\]
has oscillation at most \(e\) on each cell. Evaluating every node to a rational error budget divided by the resulting finite number of operations gives sound finite infimum, supremum, and trapezoidal-integral enclosures. The required computation consists of \(N_{\mathrm{mesh}}+1\) node calls, the displayed Taylor cutoffs, square-root bisection cutoffs, and finitely many endpoint operations. The absolute value of a real interval is implemented by the square-free endpoint rule implicit in \(\operatorname{sq}_{-}\) and \(\operatorname{sq}_{+}\), and has the same compositional modulus property.

A concrete implementation discharges \(\mathsf{CCIA}_{\mathrm{build}}\) by implementing these algorithms, exporting their soundness and effective-modulus contracts, and compiling the resulting module. Later executable conclusions are conditional on a build satisfying this specification.

73c5acf0accbde1432adb6b4c4b1ed6f3c6b52c4.title: Adaptive contour estimator \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\)
73c5acf0accbde1432adb6b4c4b1ed6f3c6b52c4.body:
The statistic \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}\) is defined from the sample \((T_i,Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\), the clipped treatment code \(\bar g_n\), the primitive parameters \(p\), and the fixed contour-bank data \(\mathfrak p_{\star},\mathfrak c_{\theta,\star}\) as follows.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Form the residualized treatments
\[
Z_{n,i}=T_i-\bar g_n(X_i),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]

\item For each fold \(a\in\{0,1\}\), each derivative order indicated below, and each complex argument \(z\), define the empirical transforms
\[
\widehat F_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
=
|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Z_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
\qquad p\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
and
\[
\widehat G_{a,n}^{(p)}(z)
=
|I_a|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_a}Y_iZ_{n,i}^{p}e^{zZ_{n,i}},
\qquad p\in\{0,1\}.
\]

\item Let the contour bank associated with \(\mathfrak p_{\star}\) provide circles \(C_j\) of radii \(\rho_j\), and parametrize each circle by
\[
z_j(t)=\rho_je^{2\pi it},
\qquad 0\le t\le1.
\]
For the pilot fold define
\[
W_{0j}(t)=
\rho_je^{2\pi it}
\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z_j(t))}
     {\widehat F_{0,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
For the evaluation fold define
\[
V_j(t)=
\rho_je^{2\pi it}
\frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z_j(t))}
     {\widehat F_{1,n}(z_j(t))}.
\]
The integrand \(V_j\) is unnormalized at this stage; the zero count \(N_j\) divides the finished contour integral.

\item Using rational upper magnitude bounds \(U_{Z,i}\), \(U_{Y,i}\), and \(U_{\rho,j}\), together with \(e^x\le3^{\lceil x\rceil}\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\pi<4\), compute rational supremum bounds for the empirical derivative sums. If \(m>0\) is a rational lower bound for the denominator modulus on \(C_j\), use
\[
|W'_{0j}(t)|\le
64\left[
\rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|}{m}
+\rho_j^2\left\{
\frac{\sup|\widehat F''_{0,n}|}{m}
+\frac{\sup|\widehat F'_{0,n}|^2}{m^2}
\right\}\right],
\]
and
\[
|V'_j(t)|\le
64\left[
\rho_j\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|}{m}
+\rho_j^2\left\{
\frac{\sup|\widehat G'_{1,n}|}{m}
+\frac{\sup|\widehat G_{1,n}|\sup|\widehat F'_{1,n}|}{m^2}
\right\}\right].
\]
For rational tolerance \(e>0\) and any resulting rational Lipschitz bound \(L\), use the mesh size
\[
\lceil L/e\rceil+1.
\]

\item On the pilot fold, for every \(j\), compute an interval of width at most \(a_{\star}/64\) enclosing
\[
\inf_{z\in C_j}|\widehat F_{0,n}(z)|.
\]
Let \(m_j\) be its lower endpoint. If \(m_j>0\), enclose
\[
\int_0^1W_{0j}(t)\,dt
=
\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
\frac{\widehat F'_{0,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{0,n}(z)}\,dz
\]
in a complex rectangle whose coordinate widths are strictly below \(1/4\). Define \(N_j\) as the unique nonnegative integer contained in the real interval when the imaginary interval contains zero; otherwise reject \(C_j\). The admissible contours are exactly those satisfying
\[
m_j\ge a_{\star}/2,
\qquad
N_j\ge1.
\]
Select an admissible contour with greatest lower endpoint \(m_j\), using the smallest index as tie-break. If the admissible set is empty, output the zero value.

\item On the evaluation fold for the selected contour \(C_j\), compute the analogous denominator-modulus lower endpoint. If it is below \(a_{\star}/4\), output the zero value. Otherwise enclose the unnormalized integral
\[
\int_0^1V_j(t)\,dt
=
\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
\frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]
After division by \(N_j\), obtain a rectangle of coordinate radius at most \(1/n\) enclosing
\[
\frac{1}{N_j2\pi i}\oint_{C_j}
\frac{\widehat G_{1,n}(z)}{\widehat F_{1,n}(z)}\,dz.
\]

\item Let \(y\in\mathbb Q\) be the midpoint of the real interval from the normalized rectangle. The output statistic is
\[
\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{spec},n}
=
\operatorname{clip}_{C_{\theta}}(y)
=
\frac{|y+C_{\theta}|-|y-C_{\theta}|}{2}
=
\Pi_{[-C_{\theta},C_{\theta}]}(y).
\]
\end{enumerate}

The parameter record \(p\) has \(n\ge1\), natural numbers \(r,k\) with \(k=r+1\) and \(2\le r\), \(s\in[0,\infty]\) with \(r\le s\), \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), strictly positive constants \(C_{\theta},C_g,C_q,\psi_{\eta},\psi_{\xi},\delta,\sigma\), and nonnegative nonincreasing sequences \(\varepsilon_{1n},\varepsilon_{2n}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\) on positive indices. The contour-bank data satisfy
\[
R_0=A_k\left(\frac{\psi_{\eta}^2}{\delta}\right)^{(k-2)^{-1}},
\qquad
R_1=R_0+1,
\]
with the natural-number field equal to \(k\) and the positive represented fields corresponding to \(\delta\), \(\psi_{\eta}\), \(R_0\), and \(R_1\). The range data correspond to \(C_{\theta}\). For ordinary real inputs, the coordinates may be canonically represented by
\[
\mathcal I_m(x)=
\left[
2^{-m}\lfloor2^m x\rfloor,
2^{-m}\{\lfloor2^m x\rfloor+1\}
\right],
\qquad m\ge1.
\]
The represented-data implementation takes supplied digital approximations of \(T_i\), \(Y_i\), and \(\bar g_n(X_i)\), adjoins the same fixed primitive components, and returns the same rational output and clipped value as the ordinary construction when applied to these canonical inputs.

8afdef3693983c90cab848c9e92a898af5b46dca.title: Local-to-Gaussian frontier
8afdef3693983c90cab848c9e92a898af5b46dca.body:
A natural next question concerns triangular treatment-noise laws satisfying
\[
|\kappa_k(\eta_n)|\ge\delta_n,
\qquad
\delta_n\downarrow0,
\]
under the same supplied code sequences. It remains open whether a data-driven selector among ordinary DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour procedures can attain the sharp minimax mean-squared-error rate as a function of
\[
(n,\varepsilon_{1,n},\varepsilon_{2,n},\delta_n),
\]
yield uniformly valid inference across these regimes, and admit a matching local minimax lower bound.
